sentences.zh: 苻堅

translations.literal: Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: ，堅饗群臣於前殿，樂奏賦詩。

translations.literal: , Jian feasted the host of ministers in the front hall; music was performed and they composed odes.
translations.idiomatic: In the front hall Fu Jian feasted his ministers while musicians played and the company composed verse.

sentences.zh: 秦州別駕天水姜平子詩有「丁」字，直而不曲。

translations.literal: The Qinzhou regional inspector's aide Jiang Pingzi of Tianshui had in his poem the graph ding, written straight and not curved.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Pingzi, who served as aide to the Qinzhou regional inspector, wrote a poem in which the character ding appeared with straight strokes, never bending.

sentences.zh: 堅問其故，平子曰：「臣丁至剛，不可以屈，且曲下者之不正之物，未足獻也。

translations.literal: Jian asked the reason. Pingzi said, "Your subject's ding is utmost hardness and cannot be bent; moreover what lies beneath a curve is something improper—not fit to be offered."
translations.idiomatic: When Jian pressed him, Pingzi answered that ding stood for unyielding firmness, that anything that bent downward was morally crooked, and therefore unworthy to present.

sentences.zh: 」堅笑曰：「名不虛行。

translations.literal: " Jian laughed and said, "The name is not borne in vain."
translations.idiomatic: Jian laughed and replied that the man's reputation matched his clever excuse.

sentences.zh: 」因擢為上第。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ranked him in the highest class.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon placed him in the top grade of the examination.

sentences.zh: 堅兄法子東海公陽與王猛子散騎侍郎皮謀反，事泄，堅問反狀，陽曰：「《禮》雲，父母之仇，不同天地。

translations.literal: Jian's cousin, Duke Yang of the East Sea—son of Fu Fa—and Pi, son of Wang Meng and holder of the post of attendant cavalry gentleman, plotted rebellion; the matter leaked out. Jian asked the circumstances of their revolt. Yang said, "The Book of Rites says: the enemy of father and mother is not one you share the world with."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yang, heir of Fu Fa's ducal line in the east, conspired with Wang Pi, Wang Meng's son and a scattered-cavalry attendant; when the plot was exposed, Jian demanded an explanation. Yang quoted the canonical rule that a son must avenge a slain parent.

sentences.zh: 臣父哀公，死不以罪，齊襄復九世之仇，而況臣也！

translations.literal: "My father, posthumously honored as Duke Ai, died though innocent; Duke Huan of Qi avenged a grievance nine generations old—how much more may your subject!"
translations.idiomatic: He insisted that his father had been wronged to death and that even a blood feud many generations deep deserved redress, let alone his own case.

sentences.zh: 」皮曰：「臣父丞相有佐命之勳，而臣不免貧餒，所以圖富也。

translations.literal: " Pi said, "My father the chancellor had merit in aiding the founding mandate, yet your subject could not escape poverty and hunger; that is why I sought riches."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi answered more plainly that he had plotted for wealth because his family, despite his father's service, still lived in want.

sentences.zh: 」堅流涕謂陽曰：「哀公之薨，事不在朕，卿寧不知之！

translations.literal: " Jian wept and said to Yang, "Duke Ai's death was not due to Us—can you truly not know it!"
translations.idiomatic: Jian wept as he told Yang that he was not responsible for Duke Ai's death and that Yang knew it.

sentences.zh: 」讓皮曰：「丞相臨終，托卿以十具牛為田，不聞為卿求位。

translations.literal: Reproaching Pi, he said, "When the chancellor died he left you ten teams of oxen for farming; We did not hear that he sought office for you."
translations.idiomatic: Turning to Pi, he reminded him that Wang Meng's dying gift had been draft oxen for the plow, not a bid for rank.

sentences.zh: 知子莫若父，何斯言之征也！

translations.literal: "No one knows a son like the father—how true those words ring!"
translations.idiomatic: He added that a father knows his son best, and Wang Meng's judgment had proved painfully accurate.

sentences.zh: 」皆赦不誅，徙陽于高昌，皮于朔方之北。

translations.literal: " All were pardoned and not executed; Yang was banished to Gaochang and Pi to the region north of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he spared them both, exiling Yang to Gaochang and Pi beyond Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 苻融以位忝宗正，不能肅遏奸萌，上疏請待罪私籓。

translations.literal: Fu Rong, ashamed that his post as director of the imperial clan had failed to check treason at its root, submitted a memorial asking to await punishment in his private princedom.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong, mortified that treason had sprouted on his watch as imperial-clan intendant, offered to accept demotion and wait out his disgrace in his own fief.

sentences.zh: 堅不許。

translations.literal: Jian did not grant permission.
translations.idiomatic: Jian refused the request.

sentences.zh: 將以融為司徒，融固辭。

translations.literal: He was about to appoint Rong minister of education, but Rong firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He had intended to make Fu Rong minister of education, but Fu Rong steadfastly declined.

sentences.zh: 堅銳意荊、揚，將謀入寇，乃改授融征南大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Jian was intent on Jingzhou and Yangzhou and planned a southward invasion, so he instead appointed Rong general who conquers the south, commissioner with extraordinary powers, and ceremonially equal to the three excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Determined to strike south toward the Jin heartland, Jian reassigned him as general who conquers the south with full staff privileges matching the three highest ministers.

sentences.zh: 新平郡獻玉器。

translations.literal: Xinping commandery presented jade ritual vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery of Xinping sent forward jade implements fit for a Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 初，堅即偽位，新平王彫陳說圖讖，堅大悅，以彫為太史令。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jian first took the usurped throne, Wang Diao of Xinping presented prophetic charts and registers; Jian was greatly pleased and appointed Diao court astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian had first seized the throne, Wang Diao of Xinping had flattered him with apocryphal prophecies; delighted, Jian put him in charge of the astrological office.

sentences.zh: 嘗言於堅曰：「謹案讖云：'古月之末亂中州，洪水大起健西流，惟有雄子定八州。

translations.literal: He once said to Jian, "Your subject has respectfully examined the prophecy: 'At the end of the ancient moon the central plain will be thrown into chaos; great floods will rise and Jian will flow west; only the heroic son will settle the eight provinces.'"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Diao once cited a cryptic verse about turmoil in the heartland, floods, a western surge of power, and a hero who would pacify the eight provinces.

sentences.zh: '此即三祖、陛下之聖諱也。

translations.literal: 'This then decodes to the sacred taboo names of the three ancestors and Your Majesty.'
translations.idiomatic: He claimed its characters spelled the taboo names of Jian's forebears and of Jian himself.

sentences.zh: 又曰：'當有草付臣又土，滅東燕，破白虜，氐在中，華在表。

translations.literal: It also says, 'There shall be one who bears 草 beside 付 with 臣 above 又 and 土, who will destroy Eastern Yan, break the white barbarians, with the Di within and the Huah without.'
translations.idiomatic: Another line, he said, described a ruler whose name compounded the graphs for Fu and Jian, who would crush Former Yan and the steppe peoples while ordering Chinese and non-Chinese subjects.

sentences.zh: '案圖讖之文，陛下當滅燕，平六州。

translations.literal: 'Examining the charts' wording, Your Majesty ought to destroy Yan and pacify the six provinces.'
translations.idiomatic: From that same lore he argued that Jian was destined to annex Murong Yan and bring six provinces to heel.

sentences.zh: 願徙汧、隴諸氐于京師，三秦大戶置於邊地，以應圖讖之言。

translations.literal: 'I ask that the Di of the Qian and Long highlands be moved into the capital region and the great clans of the three Qin districts shifted to the frontiers, to answer the prophecy's words.'
translations.idiomatic: He urged relocating Di households to the capital and exiling powerful Qin families to the borderlands to fulfill the omens.

sentences.zh: 」堅訪之王猛，猛以彫為左道惑眾，勸堅誅之。

translations.literal: " Jian consulted Wang Meng; Meng said Diao deluded the masses with heterodox doctrine and urged Jian to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian asked Wang Meng, who dismissed Wang Diao as a charlatan and urged his execution.

sentences.zh: 彫臨刑上疏曰：「臣以趙建武四年，從京兆劉湛學，明於圖記，謂臣曰：'新平地古顓頊之墟，裏名曰雞閭。

translations.literal: Diao, facing execution, submitted a memorial: "Your subject, in the fourth year of Later Zhao's Jianwu era, studied with Liu Zhan of Jingzhao and mastered charts and records; he told your subject, 'The land of Xinping was in antiquity the ruins of Zhuanxu; there is a hamlet called Jimen (Chicken Gate).'"
translations.idiomatic: On the scaffold Wang Diao insisted that he had studied under Liu Zhan since the Later Zhao period and had learned that Xinping covered Zhuanxu's old ground and contained a hamlet called Jimen.

sentences.zh: 記雲，此裏應出帝王寶器，其名曰延壽寶鼎。

translations.literal: 'The records say that from this hamlet should come the imperial treasure vessel named the Extended-Life Treasure Tripod.'
translations.idiomatic: Prophetic writings, he said, promised a dynastic tripod called Extended Life would surface there.

sentences.zh: 顓頊有雲，河上先生為吾隱之於咸陽西北，吾之孫有草付臣又土應之。

translations.literal: 'Zhuanxu left word that the Old Man on the River hid it for me northwest of Xianyang, and that my descendant bearing 草 付 臣 又 土 would correspond to it.'
translations.idiomatic: He added a tale of Zhuanxu, a riverside hermit, and a descendant whose name matched Fu Jian's graphs.

sentences.zh: '湛又云：'吾嘗齋於室中，夜有流星大如半月，落於此地，斯蓋是乎！

translations.literal: 'Zhan also said, "I once fasted in a chamber, and at night a meteor half the size of the moon fell here—can this not be that place!"'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan, he claimed, had even seen a great meteor fall on the very spot while fasting.

sentences.zh: '願陛下志之，平七州之後，出於壬午之年。

translations.literal: 'May Your Majesty remember: after you pacify the seven provinces it will appear in a ren-wu year.'"
translations.idiomatic: He begged Jian to mark the omen and expect the tripod after seven provinces fell, in a ren-wu year.

sentences.zh: 」至是而新平人得之以獻，器銘篆書文題之法，一為天王，二為王后，三為三公，四為諸侯，五為伯子男，六為卿大夫，七為元士。

translations.literal: " At this time a man of Xinping found it and presented it; the vessel's seal-script inscription, following the titling method, read: first the heaven king, second the heaven queen, third the three excellencies, fourth the feudal lords, fifth earls, viscounts, and barons, sixth grand masters and great officers, seventh gentlemen of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward locals unearthed a jade object whose raised seal text ranked offices from king and queen down through the nobility and bureaucracy in seven tiers.

sentences.zh: 自此已下，考載文記，列帝王名臣，自天子王后，內外次序，上應天文，象紫宮布列，依玉牒版辭，不違帝王之數。

translations.literal: Below that it collated documentary glosses, arraying emperors' and ministers' names from the son of heaven and queen inward and outward in order, matching celestial patterns like the Purple Palace formation and following the jade register's phrases without violating the reckoning proper to emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Lower bands correlated sovereigns and ministers with constellations and palace layouts, as if the piece were a cosmic census cast in jade.

sentences.zh: 從上元人皇起，至中元，窮於下元，天地一變，盡三元而止。

translations.literal: From the upper-prime human sovereign through the middle prime down to exhaustion at the lower prime—one transformation of heaven and earth, ending after the full cycle of three primes.
translations.idiomatic: Its chronology ran through the three cosmic primes until the cycle closed, framing Jian's rise as cosmically timed.

sentences.zh: 堅以彫言有征，追贈光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Jian, because Diao's words had proven true, posthumously awarded him the title grand master of brilliant prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced by the "fulfilled" prophecy, Jian posthumously ennobled Wang Diao as grand master of brilliant prosperity.

sentences.zh: 幽州蝗，廣袤千里，堅遣其散騎常侍劉蘭持節為使者，發青、冀、幽、并百姓討之。

translations.literal: Locusts struck Youzhou, covering a thousand li; Jian sent his sanqi permanent attendant Liu Lan, bearing credentials as envoy, to mobilize the commoners of Qing, Ji, You, and Bing to destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: When a locust swarm blanketed Youzhou, Jian dispatched Liu Lan with imperial staff to rally the northern provinces in beating back the plague.

sentences.zh: 以苻朗為使持節、都督青徐兗三州諸軍事、鎮東將軍、青州刺史，以諫議大夫裴元略為陵江將軍、西夷校尉、巴西梓潼二郡太守，密授規模，令與王撫備舟師於蜀，將以入寇。

translations.literal: He appointed Fu Lang commissioner with extraordinary powers, area commander-in-chief for military affairs in Qing, Xu, and Yan provinces, general who garrisons the east, and inspector of Qing province; appointed remonstrance grandee Pei Yuanlue general who blocks the river, colonel of the western Yi, and administrator of the two commanderies Baxi and Zitong, secretly giving him plans to join Wang Fu in preparing riverine forces in Shu for an invasion.
translations.idiomatic: He named Fu Lang to command the eastern front toward Jin while secretly instructing Pei Yuanlue to ready a Sichuan flotilla with Wang Fu for a coordinated strike.

sentences.zh: 車師前部王彌窴、鄯善王休密馱朝於堅，堅賜以朝服，引見西堂。

translations.literal: The king of the front division of Cheshi, Mixian, and the king of Shanshan, Xiumituo, paid court to Jian; Jian bestowed court dress and received them in the west hall.
translations.idiomatic: The rulers of Cheshi and Shanshan visited Chang'an; Jian robed them as peers and received them in the western hall.

sentences.zh: 窴等觀其宮宇壯麗，儀衛嚴肅，甚懼，因請年年貢獻。

translations.literal: Mixian and the others saw the palace's splendor and the sternness of the guards and attendants; they were greatly frightened and therefore asked to offer tribute every year.
translations.idiomatic: Awed by the capital's grandeur and the discipline of the escort, they volunteered annual tribute out of fear.

sentences.zh: 堅以西域路遙，不許，令三年一貢，九年一朝，以為永制。

translations.literal: Jian, because the road to the Western Regions was long, did not permit it, ordering tribute once every three years and court audience once every nine years, as a standing rule.
translations.idiomatic: Jian deemed the Silk Road too long for yearly embassies and fixed a cycle of triennial gifts and nine-year audiences instead.

sentences.zh: 窴等請曰：「大宛諸國雖通貢獻，然誠節未純，請乞依漢置都護故事。

translations.literal: Mixian and others requested, "The states of Dayuan and the rest, though they send tribute, are not yet pure in good faith; we beg to follow the Han precedent of installing a protector-general."
translations.idiomatic: The kings pleaded for a protector-general on the Han model, arguing that western states still wavered in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 若王師出關，請為鄉導。

translations.literal: "If the royal army leaves the pass, we ask to serve as guides."
translations.idiomatic: They offered to guide Qin troops if Jian sent an army beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 」堅於是以驍騎呂光為持節、都督西討諸軍事，與陵江將軍姜飛、輕騎將軍彭晃等配兵七萬，以討定西域。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Jian made Lu Guang of the ferocious cavalry commissioner with extraordinary powers, area commander-in-chief for the western expedition, together with general who blocks the river Jiang Fei, general of light cavalry Peng Huang, and others, assigning seventy thousand troops to campaign west and pacify the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Jian therefore gave Lu Guang seventy thousand men, with Jiang Fei and Peng Huang as subordinates, to subdue the Tarim states.

sentences.zh: 苻融以虛秏中國，投兵萬里之外，得其人不可役，得其地不可耕，固諫以為不可。

translations.literal: Fu Rong argued that this would hollowly exhaust the central plain and cast armies beyond ten thousand li—captured peoples could not be levied for corvée and captured lands could not be farmed—and firmly remonstrated that it must not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong warned that a far-western war would drain the core territories for gains neither taxable nor arable.

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「二漢力不能制匈奴，猶出師西域。

translations.literal: Jian said, "The two Han could not subdue the Xiongnu yet still sent armies to the Western Regions."
translations.idiomatic: Jian replied that even the weak Eastern and Western Han had projected force westward despite Xiongnu pressure.

sentences.zh: 今匈奴既平，易若摧朽，雖勞師遠役，可傳檄而定，化被昆山，垂芳千載，不亦美哉！

translations.literal: "Now the Xiongnu are already pacified; crushing the west is easier than smashing dry rot; though the army labors on a distant campaign, it can be settled with a single proclamation—transforming even Mount Kunlun, leaving fragrance for a thousand ages—is not this beautiful!"
translations.idiomatic: With the steppe quiet, he boasted that a proclamation could finish the job and win him immortal fame as far as Kunlun.

sentences.zh: 」朝臣又屢諫，皆不納。

translations.literal: Court ministers remonstrated repeatedly; none of it was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The court objected again and again; Jian brushed every warning aside.

sentences.zh: 晉將軍朱綽焚踐沔北屯田，掠六百餘戶而還。

translations.literal: Jin general Zhu Chuo burned and trampled the military colonies north of the Mian River, plundered more than six hundred households, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: A Jin column under Zhu Chuo ravaged Qin's Han River colonies, carrying off six hundred-odd households.

sentences.zh: 堅引群臣會議，曰：「吾統承大業垂二十載，芟夷逋穢，四方略定，惟東南一隅未賓王化。

translations.literal: Jian summoned the host of ministers and said, "We have upheld the great enterprise for nearly twenty years, cut down fugitive filth, and the four quarters are largely settled; only the southeastern corner has not submitted to royal transformation."
translations.idiomatic: At court he declared that after two decades of conquest only the southeast still resisted his mandate.

sentences.zh: 吾每思天下不一，未嘗不臨食輟餔，今欲起天下兵以討之。

translations.literal: "Whenever We think that the realm is not one, We never fail to set down Our spoon at the meal; now We wish to raise the hosts of the realm to punish them."
translations.idiomatic: He said the thought of a divided empire stole his appetite and that he meant to mobilize the whole realm against Jin.

sentences.zh: 略計兵杖精卒，可有九十七萬，吾將躬先啟行，薄伐南裔，于諸卿意何如？

translations.literal: "Roughly counting crack troops and arms, there may be nine hundred seventy thousand; We will take the van in person and chastise the southern frontier—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: He claimed nine hundred seventy thousand effectives and asked whether he should personally lead the southern thrust.

sentences.zh: 」秘書監硃彤曰：「陛下應天順時，恭行天罰，嘯吒則五嶽摧覆，呼吸則江海絕流，若一舉百萬，必有征無戰。

translations.literal: Secretary supervisor Zhu Tong said, "Your Majesty accords with Heaven and the seasons and respectfully executes Heaven's punishment; a shout and the five marchmounts would crumble, a breath and the rivers and seas would cut off their flow.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tong flattered him with cosmic hyperbole about his power to shake mountains and dry rivers with a word.

sentences.zh: 晉主自當銜璧輿櫬，啟顙軍門，若迷而弗悟，必逃死江海，猛將追之，即可賜命南巢。

translations.literal: "If in one stroke You raise a million men, there will be campaigns without battles. The Jin ruler will of himself bind jade disks to his neck and coffin boards to his back, knock his forehead at the army gate; if he strays and does not awaken, he must flee to die on the rivers and seas—Your fierce generals pursue him—and You may grant him his fate south of the Chao nest.
translations.idiomatic: He predicted that Emperor Xiaowu would surrender at once or flee to a watery grave while Qin pursuers finished him south of Lake Chao.

sentences.zh: 中州之人，還之桑梓。

translations.literal: "The people of the central plain will be returned to their mulberry-and-catalpa homes."
translations.idiomatic: He promised to repatriate northerners to their old homesteads.

sentences.zh: 然後回駕岱宗，告成封禪，起白雲於中壇，受萬歲於中嶽，爾則終古一時，書契未有。

translations.literal: "Then You will turn Your carriage to Mount Tai, report success and perform the Feng and Shan sacrifices, raise the white cloud at the middle altar, receive the myriad-years praise upon the central marchmount—then for once since eternity there will be something no written record has seen."
translations.idiomatic: He closed with a vision of Feng-Shan rites on Mount Tai and an ageless triumph without precedent in the annals.

sentences.zh: 」堅大悅曰：「吾之志也。

translations.literal: " Jian was greatly pleased and said, "That is Our purpose."
translations.idiomatic: Jian exclaimed that this was exactly his ambition.

sentences.zh: 」左僕射權翼進曰：「臣以為晉未可伐。

translations.literal: " Left cavalier attendant-in-ordinary Quan Yi stepped forward and said, "Your subject holds that Jin must not be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yi answered that Jin should not be invaded.

sentences.zh: 夫以紂之無道，天下離心，八百諸侯不謀而至，武王猶曰彼有人焉，回師止旆。

translations.literal: For though King Zhou of Shang lacked the Way, the realm turned its back; eight hundred lords came without prior plan—yet King Wu still said that they had men there, and turned the army and halted the banners.
translations.idiomatic: He cited King Wu's hesitation even when Shang was tottering and vassals flocked to him without prior coordination.

sentences.zh: 三仁誅放，然後奮戈牧野。

translations.literal: Only after the three worthies were killed or banished did he raise the halberd at Muye.
translations.idiomatic: Wu struck only after dispatching Shang's loyal ministers.

sentences.zh: 今晉道雖微，未聞喪德，君臣和睦，上下同心。

translations.literal: Now though the way of Jin is feeble, We have not heard that its virtue is lost; ruler and ministers are in harmony, and above and below are of one mind.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, he argued, showed no comparable moral collapse; court and country still pulled together.

sentences.zh: 謝安、桓沖，江表偉才，可謂晉有人焉。

translations.literal: Xie An and Huan Chong are great talents across the Yangtze—one may say Jin has men there.
translations.idiomatic: Figures such as Xie An and Huan Chong proved that the east still had statesmen of stature.

sentences.zh: 臣聞師克在和，今晉和矣，未可圖也。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that armies prevail in harmony; now Jin is in harmony—it cannot be plotted against.
translations.idiomatic: Because armies win through inner unity, and Jin enjoyed that unity, the time was wrong for Qin.

sentences.zh: 」堅默然久之，曰：「諸君各言其志。

translations.literal: " Jian was silent a long time, then said, "Each of you may state his mind."
translations.idiomatic: Jian fell silent, then invited every minister to speak freely.

sentences.zh: 」太子左衛率石越對曰：「吳人恃險偏隅，不賓王命，陛下親禦六師，問罪衡、越，誠合人神四海之望。

translations.literal: Shi Yue, senior commandant of the heir apparent's household guard, replied, "The people of Wu rely on their terrain in a remote corner and do not obey the royal command; if Your Majesty personally controls the six hosts and calls the south to account from Jing-Heng to Yang-Yue, it truly fits the hope of gods and men within the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yue conceded that a personal expedition against the southern enclave would gratify gods and men alike.

sentences.zh: 但今歲鎮星守斗牛，福德有吳。

translations.literal: Yet this year the year star guards Dipper and Ox, and the virtue of blessings lies with Wu.
translations.idiomatic: But astrology, he warned, favored the southeast: the year star hung over the Jin sector.

sentences.zh: 懸象無差，弗可犯也。

translations.literal: The suspended images are without error—they must not be violated.
translations.idiomatic: He insisted that stellar signs were not to be defied.

sentences.zh: 且晉中宗，籓王耳，夷夏之情，咸共推之，遺愛猶在於人。

translations.literal: Moreover Emperor Yuan of Jin was a imperial clansman, and barbarian and Chinese alike supported him; his lingering kindness still endures among the people.
translations.idiomatic: He reminded Jian that Sima Rui had been widely accepted, Chinese and non-Chinese, and his memory still endeared the house of Jin.

sentences.zh: 昌明，其孫也，國有長江之險，朝無昏貳之釁。

translations.literal: Changming is his grandson; the state has the Yangtze as its bulwark, and at court there is no twilight defect born of palace intrigue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu, he noted, was Yuan's lineal descendant, the Yangtze shielded the dynasty, and the palace showed no Consort Dusk-style corruption.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為利用修德，未宜動師。

translations.literal: Your stupid subject therefore holds that the right course is to cultivate virtue and that it is not yet time to move the army.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yue therefore urged patience and moral suasion rather than war.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：'遠人不服，修文德以來之。

translations.literal: Confucius said, 'When those afar do not submit, cultivate civil virtue to draw them.'
translations.idiomatic: He quoted Confucius on winning distant peoples through culture rather than force.

sentences.zh: '願保境養兵，伺其虛隙。

translations.literal: 'We beg You to guard the borders, nurture the army, and watch for their gaps and weaknesses.'"
translations.idiomatic: He asked Jian to husband strength and await Jin's own mistakes.

sentences.zh: 」堅曰：「吾聞武王伐紂，逆歲犯星。

translations.literal: " Jian said, "We have heard that when King Wu attacked Zhou, he went against the year and offended the stars."
translations.idiomatic: Jian countered with King Wu's willingness to campaign even when omens were adverse.

sentences.zh: 天道幽遠，未可知也。

translations.literal: The Way of Heaven is dark and distant—not to be known.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed astrology as unknowable.

sentences.zh: 昔夫差威陵上國，而為句踐所滅。

translations.literal: In the past Fuchai overawed the central states yet was destroyed by Goujian.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Fuchai's humiliation despite dominating the north.

sentences.zh: 仲謀澤洽全吳，孫皓因三代之業，龍驤一呼，君臣面縛，雖有長江，其能固乎！

translations.literal: Zhongmou's kindness soaked all Wu; Sun Hao inherited three generations' enterprise—yet with one cry of the Dragon Prancing host ruler and ministers presented themselves bound. Though they had the Yangtze, how could it hold firm!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan's legacy and Sun Hao's inherited realm had not saved Wu from Wang Jun's fleet; a great river was no sure shield.

sentences.zh: 以吾之眾旅，投鞭于江，足斷其流。

translations.literal: "With Our many hosts, if We cast whips into the Yangtze, it is enough to dam its flow."
translations.idiomatic: He boasted that Qin soldiers could stem the river by throwing in their riding crops.

sentences.zh: 」越曰：「臣聞紂為無道，天下患之。

translations.literal: Yue said, "Your subject has heard that Zhou lacked the Way and the realm resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yue replied that tyrants fell because the world hated them.

sentences.zh: 夫差淫虐，孫皓昏暴，眾叛親離，所以敗也。

translations.literal: Fuchai was licentious and cruel; Sun Hao was dim and violent—the multitudes rebelled and kin departed; that is why they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchai and Sun Hao had lost the people through cruelty and folly.

sentences.zh: 今晉雖無德，未有斯罪，深願厲兵積粟以待天時。

translations.literal: Now though Jin lacks virtue, it has not these crimes; your subject deeply wishes You to harden the army, pile grain, and await Heaven's moment.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, he repeated, showed none of those fatal vices, so Qin should drill, store grain, and bide Heaven's hour.

sentences.zh: 」群臣各有異同，庭議者久之。

translations.literal: " The host of ministers each agreed or disagreed; the court debated for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers argued pro and con until the session wore on.

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「所謂築室於道，沮計萬端，吾當內斷於心矣。

translations.literal: Jian said, "This is what is called building a house in the road—ten thousand plans are blocked; We shall decide within Our heart."
translations.idiomatic: Jian compared their wrangling to builders arguing in the middle of a road and said he would settle the matter privately.

sentences.zh: 」群臣出後，獨留苻融議之。

translations.literal: After the host of ministers left, he kept only Fu Rong to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: When the others withdrew he kept Fu Rong alone.

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「自古大事，定策者一兩人而已，群議紛紜，徒亂人意，吾當與汝決之」融曰：「歲鎮在斗牛，吳、越之福，不可以伐一也。

translations.literal: Jian said, "Since antiquity great matters have been settled by one or two men; a host of disputation only confuses men's minds—We shall resolve it with you." Rong said, "The year star sits in Dipper and Ox—that is fortune for Wu and Yue; they must not be attacked—that is one.
translations.idiomatic: He told Fu Rong that policy belonged to a tiny circle, then heard Fu Rong's first reason: astrology favored the lower Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 晉主休明，朝臣用命，不可以伐二也。

translations.literal: The Jin ruler is enlightened and the court ministers obey commands—they must not be attacked—that is two.
translations.idiomatic: Second, the Jin court still commanded loyalty.

sentences.zh: 我數戰，兵疲將倦，有憚敵之意，不可以伐三也。

translations.literal: We have fought repeatedly; soldiers are weary and generals tired, and there is fear of the enemy—they must not be attacked—that is three.
translations.idiomatic: Third, Qin's own army was exhausted and secretly afraid.

sentences.zh: 諸言不可者，策之上也，願陛下納之。

translations.literal: Those who speak of impermissibility offer the upper strategy; I hope Your Majesty will accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong urged Jian to treat the naysayers as wise counselors.

sentences.zh: 」堅作色曰：「汝復如此，天下之事，吾當誰與言之！

translations.literal: " Jian changed color and said, "If you again speak thus, under Heaven's affairs—with whom shall We speak of them!"
translations.idiomatic: Jian flushed and demanded to know whom he could trust if not himself.

sentences.zh: 今有眾百萬，資仗如山，吾雖未稱令主，亦不為暗劣。

translations.literal: Now We have hosts in the millions and stores of weapons like mountains; though We have not yet been called a paragon ruler, We are also not dim and inferior.
translations.idiomatic: He cited his million men and mountain of arms and denied that he was a mediocre sovereign.

sentences.zh: 以累捷之威，擊垂亡之寇，何不克之有乎！

translations.literal: With the might of repeated victories to strike a foe on the verge of perishing—how could there be no victory!
translations.idiomatic: Victory over a dying foe after so many wins seemed inevitable to him.

sentences.zh: 吾終不以賊遺子孫，為宗廟社稷之憂也。

translations.literal: We will in the end not leave the bandit to Our sons and grandsons, making trouble for the altars of state and the spirits of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He vowed not to bequeath the Jin "bandit" problem to posterity or the state cult.

sentences.zh: 」融泣曰：「吳之不可伐昭然，虛勞大舉，必無功而反。

translations.literal: Rong wept and said, "That Wu must not be attacked is clear—this hollow great levy will certainly return without merit.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong wept that the southern campaign was folly sure to fail.

sentences.zh: 臣之所憂，非此而已。

translations.literal: What your subject worries about is not this alone.
translations.idiomatic: Worse dangers, he said, lay beyond a mere reverse.

sentences.zh: 陛下寵育鮮卑、羌、羯，布諸畿甸，舊人族類，斥徙遐方。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has doted on and reared the Xianbei, Qiang, and Jie, spreading them through the capital region, while the old clans have been shifted to remote places.
translations.idiomatic: He pointed to Jian's policy of settling Xianbei, Qiang, and Jie tribes around the capital while exiling older Di allies.

sentences.zh: 今傾國而去，如有風塵之變者，其如宗廟何！

translations.literal: Now You drain the whole state and go; if there should be the turmoil of wind and dust—what of the ancestral temples!
translations.idiomatic: If Jian emptied the realm on campaign, a sudden coup could endanger the ancestral shrines.

sentences.zh: 監國以弱卒數萬留守京師，鮮卑、羌、羯攢聚如林，此皆國之賊也，我之仇也。

translations.literal: The overseer of the state has but a few tens of thousands of weak troops to guard the capital, while Xianbei, Qiang, and Jie mass like a forest—these are all plunderers of the state and Our enemies.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince would guard Chang'an with feeble garrison troops while potentially hostile tribes ringed the city.

sentences.zh: 臣恐非但徒返而已，亦未必萬全。

translations.literal: Your subject fears not only a vain return but also that safety in victory is not assured.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong doubted both success abroad and security at home.

sentences.zh: 臣智識愚淺，誠不足采；

translations.literal: Your subject's wisdom and knowledge are shallow and foolish, truly unworthy of adoption.
translations.idiomatic: He disclaimed his own counsel as crude.

sentences.zh: 王景略一時奇士，陛下每擬之孔明，其臨終之言不可忘也。

translations.literal: Wang Jinglue was a singular man of his age; Your Majesty always compared him to Kongming—the words he spoke at death must not be forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wang Meng's dying advice, he insisted, deserved the respect Jian had likened to Zhuge Liang's.

sentences.zh: 」堅不納。

translations.literal: " Jian did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Jian refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 游于東苑，命沙門道安同輦。

translations.literal: He roamed the eastern park and ordered the monk Dao'an to share his carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He toured the eastern pleasure grounds and made the monk Dao'an ride beside him in the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 權翼諫曰：「臣聞天子之法駕，侍中陪乘，清道而行，進止有度。

translations.literal: Quan Yi remonstrated: "Your subject has heard that in the Son of Heaven's lawful chariot the palace attendant rides as companion, the way is cleared to proceed, and advance and halt have their measure."
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yi protested that regalia required a courtier as riding companion, cleared roads, and measured pacing—not a Buddhist cleric.

sentences.zh: 三代末主，或虧大倫，適一時之情，書惡來世。

translations.literal: The last rulers of the three dynasties sometimes injured the great human relationships, indulging a moment's whim; the documents record their evil for later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Even the final rulers of the three ancient dynasties debased fundamental ethics for passing whim, and the classics still hold their shame up to posterity.

sentences.zh: 故班姬辭輦，垂美無窮。

translations.literal: Therefore Lady Ban declined the palanquin and left a beauty that has no end.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Lady Ban of Han refused to ride beside the emperor and won praise that has never faded.

sentences.zh: 道安毀形賤士，不宜參穢神輿。

translations.literal: Dao'an has disfigured his body and is a lowly cleric; he ought not pollute the divine chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Dao'an is a tonsured commoner and has no place fouling the imperial equipage.

sentences.zh: 」堅作色曰：「安公道冥至境，德為時尊。

translations.literal: " Jian changed color and said, "Lord An has penetrated the dark utmost realm; in virtue he is honored by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Jian flushed and retorted that the monk commanded the deepest insight and commanded universal respect.

sentences.zh: 朕舉天下之重，未足以易之。

translations.literal: We might raise the weight of the whole realm and still not be enough to exchange for him.
translations.idiomatic: He insisted that not even the empire's whole weight could buy Dao'an's worth.

sentences.zh: 非公與輦之榮，此乃朕之顯也。

translations.literal: It is not glory for you to share the palanquin with him—it is Our own display."
translations.idiomatic: Having Dao'an beside him was no favor to Quan Yi, he said, but a mark of his own enlightenment.

sentences.zh: 」命翼扶安升輦，顧謂安曰：「朕將與公南游吳、越，整六師而巡狩，謁虞陵於疑嶺，瞻禹穴於會稽，泛長江，臨滄海，不亦樂乎！

translations.literal: He ordered Yi to help Dao'an ascend the palanquin, turned and said to Dao'an, "We shall roam south with you to Wu and Yue, array the six hosts for a tour of inspection, pay respects at Shun's tomb on the Yiling ridges, gaze on Yu's grotto at Kuaiji, sail the long river, and stand by the dark sea—is not this joy!"
translations.idiomatic: He made Quan Yi steady the monk into the carriage, then mused aloud about a triumphal tour to the southeast—Shun's grave, Yu's legend, the Yangtze, and the open sea—as though it were a pleasure outing.

sentences.zh: 」安曰：「陛下應天禦世，居中土而制四維，逍遙順時，以適聖躬，動則鳴鑾清道，止則神棲無為，端拱而化，與堯、舜比靈斯，何為勞身於馳騎，口倦於經略，櫛風沐雨。

translations.literal: Dao'an said, "Your Majesty responds to Heaven and governs the age, dwelling in the central soil and controlling the four cords; you roam free and follow the seasons to suit the sage's person—when you move, bells ring and the way is cleared; when you halt, the spirit rests in non-action; you sit upright with folded hands and transform all, matching Yao and Shun in numinous virtue—why toil the person in galloping campaigns, weary the mouth in strategizing, comb the wind and wash in the rain,
translations.idiomatic: Dao'an answered that a true Son of Heaven should rule from the center like Yao and Shun, moving only with full ritual and governing through stillness, not by exhausting himself on campaign or exposing the court to wind and rain,

sentences.zh: 蒙塵野次乎？

translations.literal: and endure dust in wild encampments?"
translations.idiomatic: still less endure exile and life in field camps.

sentences.zh: 且東南區區，地下氣癘，虞舜遊而不返，大禹適而弗歸，何足以上勞神駕，下困蒼生。

translations.literal: Moreover the southeast is a tiny corner; underground miasma afflicts the soil—Shun toured there and did not return, Yu went there and did not come back—how can it be worth troubling the divine chariot above and wearing out the black-haired people below?
translations.idiomatic: The south-east, he added, was a small, fever-ridden basin where even sage-kings had met trouble; it hardly justified dragging the throne and the people into hardship.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：'惠此中國，以綏四方。

translations.literal: The Classic of Poetry says, 'Show kindness here in the central states, thereby to pacify the four quarters.'
translations.idiomatic: He quoted the Odes on winning the heartland through kindness.

sentences.zh: '苟文德足以懷遠，可不煩寸兵而坐賓百越。

translations.literal: If civil virtue suffices to embrace those afar, you need not trouble a single inch of blade to seat the Hundred Yue as guests."
translations.idiomatic: With true civil virtue, he argued, the southern tribes could be won without drawing a sword.

sentences.zh: 」堅曰：「非為地不廣、人不足也，但思混一六合，以濟蒼生。

translations.literal: " Jian said, "It is not that the land is not broad or the people insufficient; We only think to merge the six directions into one, thereby to deliver the black-haired people.
translations.idiomatic: Jian replied that scale was not the issue—he meant to unify the realm and save the common people.

sentences.zh: 天生蒸庶，樹之君者，所以除煩去亂，安得憚勞！

translations.literal: Heaven begat the teeming masses and set up rulers for them in order to remove vexation and eliminate chaos—how can We shrink from toil!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven had appointed rulers precisely to end turmoil, he insisted, so a ruler must not shun hardship.

sentences.zh: 朕既大運所鐘，將簡天心以行天罰。

translations.literal: We, whom the great fortune has favored, will examine Heaven's mind and carry out Heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed Heaven's mandate rested on him and authorized punitive war.

sentences.zh: 高辛有熊泉之役，唐堯有丹水之師，此皆著之前典，昭之後王。

translations.literal: Gaoxin had the campaign at Bear Spring; Tang Yao had the host at Red Water—these are written in the earlier canons and made plain to later kings.
translations.idiomatic: He cited ancient sage-kings who had still gone to war despite their virtue.

sentences.zh: 誠如公言，帝王無省方之文乎？

translations.literal: If it truly be as you say, do emperors have no texts for inspecting the regions?
translations.idiomatic: If Dao'an were right, he asked, would the classics never record royal tours?

sentences.zh: 且朕此行也，以義舉耳，使流度衣冠之胄，還其墟墳，復其桑梓，止為濟難銓才，不欲窮兵極武。

translations.literal: Moreover this expedition of Ours is a righteous undertaking: We shall let the wandering caps and gowns of gentle descent return to their mound-tombs and restore their mulberry-and-catalpa homes; We only mean to relieve distress and weigh talent, not to exhaust arms to the utmost or exhaust military force."
translations.idiomatic: He framed the invasion as a humane restoration of exiled gentry to their ancestral soil, not mere conquest.

sentences.zh: 」安曰：「若鑾駕必欲親動，猶不願遠涉江、淮，可暫幸洛陽，明授勝略，馳紙檄於丹陽，開其改迷之路。

translations.literal: Dao'an said, "If the imperial train must move in person, We still would not wish You to ford the Yangtze and Huai far away; You could for a time favor Luoyang, there openly hand down the winning plan, and gallop a paper proclamation to Danyang to open for them a road to repent their error.
translations.idiomatic: Dao'an conceded that if Jian had to move, he should stop at Luoyang and try edicts before crossing the great rivers.

sentences.zh: 如其不庭，伐之可也。

translations.literal: If they will not submit at court, then punish them—that can be done."
translations.idiomatic: War could follow only if Jin still refused allegiance.

sentences.zh: 」堅不納。

translations.literal: " Jian did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Jian would not take the advice.

sentences.zh: 先是，群臣以堅信重道安，謂安曰：「主上欲有事于東南，公何不為蒼生致一言也！

translations.literal: Earlier, the host of ministers, because Jian trusted and honored Dao'an, had said to Dao'an, "The lord above wishes to undertake affairs in the southeast—why do you not speak one word for the black-haired people!"
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers had privately begged Dao'an to intervene because they knew Jian listened to him.

sentences.zh: 」故安因此而諫。

translations.literal: Therefore Dao'an remonstrated on this account.
translations.idiomatic: That was why Dao'an had raised the protest.

sentences.zh: 苻融及尚書原紹、石越等上書面諫，前後數十，堅終不從。

translations.literal: Fu Rong together with Director of the Secretariat Yuan Shao, Shi Yue, and others submitted memorials remonstrating in person; front and back they were several tens—Jian in the end did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong, Yuan Shao, Shi Yue, and others filed dozens of face-to-face memorials; Jian ignored every one.

sentences.zh: 堅少子中山公詵有寵於堅，又諫曰：「臣聞季梁在隨，楚人憚之；

translations.literal: Jian's youngest son, Duke of Zhongshan Shen, who was favored by Jian, also remonstrated, saying, "Your subject has heard that when Ji Liang was in Sui, the men of Chu feared him;
translations.idiomatic: His young favorite Fu Shen cited wise ministers whose presence had once deterred invaders:

sentences.zh: 宮奇在虞，晉不窺兵。

translations.literal: when Gong Zhiqi was in Yu, Jin did not dare point troops.
translations.idiomatic: while Gong Zhiqi stayed in Yu, Jin had not dared raise an army.

sentences.zh: 國有人焉故也。

translations.literal: It was because the state had such men in it.
translations.idiomatic: Their states survived because wise men still served there.

sentences.zh: 及謀之不用，而亡不淹歲。

translations.literal: When their counsel went unused, destruction did not wait a full year.
translations.idiomatic: Once those counselors were ignored, those kingdoms fell within a year.

sentences.zh: 前車之覆軌，後車之明鑒。

translations.literal: The overturned rut of the front chariot is the bright mirror of the rear chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The overturned wheels ahead should warn the chariot behind.

sentences.zh: 陽平公，國之謀主，而陛下違之；

translations.literal: The Duke of Yangping is the state's chief strategist, yet Your Majesty goes against him;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong, Duke of Yangping, was Qin's chief planner—yet Jian set his counsel aside.

sentences.zh: 晉有謝安、桓沖，而陛下伐之。

translations.literal: Jin has Xie An and Huan Chong, yet Your Majesty attacks them.
translations.idiomatic: Jin still had Xie An and Huan Chong, yet Jian meant to strike.

sentences.zh: 是行也，臣竊惑焉。

translations.literal: On this expedition your stupid subject is privately perplexed."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shen confessed he could not fathom the campaign.

sentences.zh: 」堅曰：「國有元龜。

translations.literal: " Jian said, "The state has the great tortoise;
translations.idiomatic: Jian snapped that the realm possessed the oracle bone,

sentences.zh: 可以決大謀；

translations.literal: it can decide great plans;
translations.idiomatic: enough to settle grand strategy,

sentences.zh: 朝有公卿，可以定進否。

translations.literal: at court there are the excellencies—they can settle advance or withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: while the high ministers could judge whether to march or halt.

sentences.zh: 孺子言焉，將為戮也。」

translations.literal: When a child speaks thus, he shall be executed."
translations.idiomatic: Boys who talked that way, he warned, earned the death stroke.

sentences.zh: 所司奏劉蘭討蝗幽州，經秋冬不滅，請征下廷尉詔獄。

translations.literal: The responsible offices memorialized that Liu Lan's locust suppression in Youzhou, having passed autumn and winter, had not destroyed them, and asked to summon him down to the minister of justice's imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Officials impeached Liu Lan for failing to stop the locusts after two seasons and demanded he face imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「災降自天，殆非人力所能除也。

translations.literal: Jian said, "The calamity descended from Heaven; probably it is not what human power can remove.
translations.idiomatic: Jian replied that the plague came from Heaven and lay beyond human remedy.

sentences.zh: 此自朕之政違所致，蘭何罪焉！」

translations.literal: This derives from Our government's deviation—what crime has Lan!"
translations.idiomatic: If policy was to blame, he said, Liu Lan was innocent.

sentences.zh: 明年，呂光發長安，堅送于建章宮，謂光曰：「西戎荒俗，非禮義之邦。

translations.literal: The next year, when Lu Guang set out from Chang'an, Jian saw him off at Jianzhang Palace and said to Guang, "The western Rong are wild customs, not a land of ritual and right.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Jian escorted Lu Guang from Jianzhang and warned that the western barbarians knew no Chinese rites.

sentences.zh: 羈縻之道，服而赦之，示以中國之威，導以王化之法，勿極武窮兵，過深殘掠。

translations.literal: The way of loose reins is: submit and pardon them; display to them the majesty of the central states and guide them with the methods of royal transformation—do not exhaust arms to the utmost or campaign to the limit, going too deep in slaughter and plunder."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a policy of submission and pardon, showing imperial prestige and spreading moral instruction without needless slaughter.

sentences.zh: 」加鄯善王休密馱使持節、散騎常侍、都督西域諸軍事、甯西將軍，車師前部王彌窴使持節、平西將軍、西域都護，率其國兵為光鄉導。

translations.literal: " He added titles for the king of Shanshan, Xiumituo—commissioner with extraordinary powers, sanqi permanent attendant, area commander-in-chief of military affairs in the Western Regions, general who pacifies the west—and for the king of the front division of Cheshi, Mixian—commissioner with extraordinary powers, general who pacifies the west, protector-general of the Western Regions—to lead their state troops as guides for Guang.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted the western kings with full military titles so their troops could guide Lu Guang.

sentences.zh: 是年，益州西南夷、海南諸國皆遣使貢其方物。

translations.literal: That year the southwestern Yi of Yizhou and the various states beyond the southern sea all sent envoys presenting their local products.
translations.idiomatic: The same year tribes southwest of Yizhou and states across the southern ocean sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 堅南遊灞上，從容謂群臣曰：「軒轅，大聖也，其仁若天，其智若神，猶隨不順者從而征之，居無常所，以兵為衛，故能日月所照，風雨所至，莫不率從。

translations.literal: Jian toured south to Bashang and, at ease, said to the host of ministers, "The Yellow Thearch was a great sage; his benevolence was like Heaven, his wisdom like spirit—yet he still followed and punished those who would not submit, dwelt without a constant place, and took arms as his guard; therefore wherever sun and moon shone and wind and rain reached, none failed to follow."
translations.idiomatic: On the Bashang parade ground Jian likened himself to the Yellow Emperor, who had never ceased mobile campaigning until all under heaven obeyed.

sentences.zh: 今天下垂平，惟東南未殄。

translations.literal: Now the realm hangs almost level; only the southeast is not yet extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed the empire was nearly pacified except for the southeast.

sentences.zh: 朕忝荷大業，巨責攸歸，豈敢優遊卒歲，不建大同之業！

translations.literal: We, shamed to bear the great enterprise, with the vast charge returning to Us—how dare We idle away the year in ease and not build the enterprise of great unity!
translations.idiomatic: He said he could not idle while unification remained undone.

sentences.zh: 每思桓溫之寇也，江東不可不滅。

translations.literal: Whenever We think of Huan Wen's invasions, the lands east of the river must be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Each memory of Huan Wen's northern raids convinced him that Jiangdong had to fall.

sentences.zh: 今有勁卒百萬，文武如林，鼓行而摧遺晉，若商風之隕秋籜。

translations.literal: Now We have crack troops in the millions, civil and military like a forest; if We beat drums and march to crush remnant Jin, it will be like the autumn wind stripping autumn bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: A million veterans, he boasted, would scatter Jin like wind stripping leaves.

sentences.zh: 朝廷內外，皆言不可，吾實未解所由。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court all say it cannot be done; We truly do not understand the reason.
translations.idiomatic: He professed bafflement that everyone opposed him.

sentences.zh: 晉武若信朝士之言而不征吳者，天下何由一軌！

translations.literal: If Jin Wu had trusted the court gentlemen's words and not campaigned against Wu, by what path would the realm have been brought onto one track!
translations.idiomatic: He asked how Sima Yan could have reunified China had he listened to pacifists.

sentences.zh: 吾計決矣，不復與諸卿議也。

translations.literal: Our plan is decided; We will not debate again with you gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: He closed debate and declared the decision final.

sentences.zh: 」太子宏進曰：「吳今得歲，不可伐也。

translations.literal: " The heir apparent Hong stepped forward and said, "Wu now obtains the year star; it must not be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Fu Hong warned that astrology favored the enemy,

sentences.zh: 且晉主無罪，人為之用；

translations.literal: Moreover the Jin ruler is without crime and men work for him;
translations.idiomatic: that the Jin emperor had committed no offense and still commanded loyalty,

sentences.zh: 謝安、桓沖兄弟皆一方之俊才，君臣戮力，阻險長江，未可圖也。

translations.literal: Xie An and the Huan Chong brothers are each outstanding talents of their region; ruler and ministers join strength and block the danger of the long river—they cannot be plotted against.
translations.idiomatic: and that Xie An and the Huan brothers, defending the Yangtze, were not easy prey.

sentences.zh: 但可厲兵積粟，以待暴主，一舉而滅之。

translations.literal: You need only harden the army and pile grain to await a violent ruler, then in one stroke destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Jian to wait for Jin to produce a tyrant, then strike once.

sentences.zh: 今若動而無功，則威名損於外，資財竭於內。

translations.literal: Now if you move and have no success, then prestige and name will be damaged abroad and resources exhausted within.
translations.idiomatic: A failed campaign now would cost prestige abroad and treasure at home.

sentences.zh: 是故聖王之行師也，內斷必誠，然後用之。

translations.literal: Therefore when sage kings move hosts, they decide within with perfect sincerity, then use them.
translations.idiomatic: Sage kings, he said, marched only after unshakable inner resolve.

sentences.zh: 彼若憑長江以固守，徙江北百姓于江南，增城清野，杜門不戰，我已疲矣，彼未引弓。

translations.literal: If they rely on the long river to hold firm, relocate the people north of the river to south of the river, heighten walls and clear the fields, shut gates and refuse battle, We will already be weary while they have not yet drawn the bow.
translations.idiomatic: Jin could fortify the south bank, evacuate northerners, and refuse battle until Qin collapsed from exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 土下氣癘，不可久留，陛下將若之何？

translations.literal: Miasma afflicts the soil above and below; you cannot long remain—what will Your Majesty do then?"
translations.idiomatic: The southern climate alone, he warned, could not sustain a long siege.

sentences.zh: 」堅曰：「往年車騎滅燕，亦犯歲而捷之。

translations.literal: " Jian said, "In former years the chariot-and-horse host destroyed Yan though it offended the year star and still won.
translations.idiomatic: Jian answered with Fu Rong's earlier victory over Former Yan despite bad omens.

sentences.zh: 天道幽遠，非汝所知也。

translations.literal: The Way of Heaven is dark and distant—not something you can know.
translations.idiomatic: He again dismissed astrology as unknowable.

sentences.zh: 昔始皇之滅六國，其王豈皆暴乎？

translations.literal: In the past when the First Emperor destroyed the six states, were their kings all violent?
translations.idiomatic: He asked whether every conquered king of Qin Shihuang's era had been a tyrant.

sentences.zh: 且吾內斷於心久矣，舉必克之，何為無功！

translations.literal: Moreover We have long decided within Our heart; when We raise them We must overcome them—how could there be no success!
translations.idiomatic: He insisted his mind was made up and victory assured.

sentences.zh: 吾方命蠻夷以攻其內，精甲勁兵以攻其外，內外如此，安有不克！

translations.literal: We are about to order the barbarians to attack them within and crack armored picked troops to attack them without—with inner and outer pressure thus, how could there be no victory!"
translations.idiomatic: He planned to use internal fifth columns and external assault together.

sentences.zh: 」道安曰：「太子之言是也，願陛下納之。

translations.literal: " Dao'an said, "The heir apparent's words are right; We beg Your Majesty to accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Dao'an endorsed the crown prince,

sentences.zh: 」堅弗從。

translations.literal: " Jian would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: but Jian still refused.

sentences.zh: 冠軍慕容垂言於堅曰：「陛下德侔軒、唐，功高湯、武，威澤被於八表，遠夷重譯而歸。

translations.literal: Champion general Murong Chui said to Jian, "Your Majesty's virtue matches that of the Yellow Thearch and Tang Yao, your merit rises above Tang and Wu; awe and kindness soak the eight outer regions, and distant barbarians come again and again through interpreters.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui flattered Jian as surpassing the sage founders and drawing tribute from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 司馬昌明因餘燼之資，敢距王命，是而不誅，法將安措！

translations.literal: Sima Changming, relying on the embers that remain, dares to resist the royal command—if this be allowed and not punished, where will the law be placed!
translations.idiomatic: He denounced Emperor Xiaowu for defying Heaven's anointed conqueror.

sentences.zh: 孫氏跨僭江東，終並于晉，其勢然也。

translations.literal: The Sun house wrongly seized the lands east of the river and in the end was merged into Jin—that was the tendency of the situation.
translations.idiomatic: He said Sun Quan's separatist state had inevitably fallen to Jin,

sentences.zh: 臣聞小不敵大，弱不禦強，況大秦之應符，陛下之聖武，強兵百萬，韓、白盈朝，而令其偷魂假號，以賊虜遺子孫哉！

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the small does not match the great, the weak cannot withstand the strong—how much more when Great Qin answers the talisman and Your Majesty is sagely martial, with a million strong troops and Han Xin and Bai Qi filling the court—shall we let them steal breath and borrow titles, leaving bandit captives to sons and grandsons!
translations.idiomatic: and argued that mighty Qin could not leave a rump Jin for posterity.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：'築室於道謀，是用不潰于成。

translations.literal: The Classic of Poetry says, 'When you build a house on the road and take counsel there, you therefore cannot complete the work.'
translations.idiomatic: He quoted the Odes against deciding policy in public confusion,

sentences.zh: '陛下內斷神謀足矣，不煩廣訪朝臣以亂聖慮。

translations.literal: 'Your Majesty's inner decision and divine plan suffice; there is no need broadly to consult court ministers and confuse the sage's thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: urging Jian to trust his own secret counsel alone,

sentences.zh: 昔晉武之平吳也，言可者張、杜數賢而已，若采群臣之言，豈能建不世之功！

translations.literal: In the past when Jin Wu pacified Wu, those who said it could be done were only a few worthies such as Zhang and Du—if he had adopted the host of ministers' words, how could he have built an achievement unmatched in the age!
translations.idiomatic: citing how Sima Yan had ignored the crowd and listened to Zhang Hua and Du Yu.

sentences.zh: 諺雲憑天俟時，時已至矣，其可已乎！

translations.literal: The proverb says, rely on Heaven and await the season—the season has arrived; can it be stopped!"
translations.idiomatic: He closed with a proverb: Heaven's hour had come.

sentences.zh: 」堅大悅，曰：「與吾定天下者，其惟卿耳。

translations.literal: " Jian was greatly pleased and said, "He who will settle the realm with Us—perhaps it is you alone.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Jian told Murong Chui that only he truly shared the vision of conquest.

sentences.zh: 」賜帛五百匹。

translations.literal: " He bestowed five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded him with five hundred rolls of silk.

sentences.zh: 彗星掃東井。

translations.literal: A comet swept across the Eastern Well constellation.
translations.idiomatic: A comet trailed across the eastern well of the sky.

sentences.zh: 自堅之四月，長安有水影，遠觀若水，視地則見人，至是則止。

translations.literal: From the fourth month of Jian's reign year, at Chang'an there were watery reflections; from afar they looked like water, but looking at the ground one saw people; by this time they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: For months Chang'an had shimmered with phantom floods that resolved into human shapes when approached—omens that ended only now.

sentences.zh: 堅惡之。

translations.literal: Jian detested them.
translations.idiomatic: Jian found the omens ominous.

sentences.zh: 上林竹死，洛陽地陷。

translations.literal: Bamboo in the Shanglin Park died; the ground in Luoyang sank.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial park bamboo withered and Luoyang's earth gaped open—further ill signs.

sentences.zh: 晉車騎將軍桓沖率眾十萬伐堅，遂攻襄陽。

translations.literal: Jin general of chariots and cavalry Huan Chong led a host of one hundred thousand to campaign against Jian and thereupon attacked Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong marched a hundred thousand Jin troops against Qin and laid siege to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 遣前將軍劉波、冠軍桓石虔、振威桓石民攻沔北諸城；

translations.literal: He sent forward general Liu Bo, champion Huan Shiqian, and general who displays might Huan Shimin to attack the cities north of the Mian;
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched columns under Liu Bo, Huan Shiqian, and Huan Shimin against the Han River towns,

sentences.zh: 輔國楊亮伐蜀，攻拔伍城，進攻涪城，龍驤胡彬攻下蔡；

translations.literal: general who aids the state Yang Liang campaigned against Shu, captured Wucheng, advanced to attack Fucheng, and dragon-prancing Hu Bin captured Xia Cai;
translations.idiomatic: while Yang Liang struck into Shu, took Wucheng, pressed Fucheng, and Hu Bin seized Xia Cai,

sentences.zh: 鷹揚郭銓攻武當；

translations.literal: general who displays the falcon Guo Quan attacked Wudang;
translations.idiomatic: and Guo Quan hit Wudang.

sentences.zh: 沖別將攻萬歲城，拔之。

translations.literal: Chong's separate column attacked Wansui city and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Another detachment stormed Wansui and carried it.

sentences.zh: 堅大怒，遣其子征南睿及冠軍慕容垂、左衛毛當率步騎五萬救襄陽，揚武張崇救武當，後將軍張蠔、步兵校尉姚萇救涪城。

translations.literal: Jian was greatly angry and sent his son the southern expedition commander Rui, together with champion Murong Chui and left guard Mao Dang, leading fifty thousand foot and horse to relieve Xiangyang; general who displays might Zhang Chong to relieve Wudang; rear general Zhang He, infantry colonel Yao Chang to relieve Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jian sent Fu Rui, Murong Chui, and Mao Dang with fifty thousand men toward Xiangyang, Zhang Chong toward Wudang, and Zhang He with Yao Chang toward Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 睿次新野，垂次鄧城。

translations.literal: Rui halted at Xinye; Chui halted at Dengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rui camped at Xinye while Murong Chui stopped at Dengcheng.

sentences.zh: 王師敗張崇于武當，掠二千餘戶而歸。

translations.literal: The royal army defeated Zhang Chong at Wudang and plundered more than two thousand households before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Jin troops routed Zhang Chong at Wudang and carried off over two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 睿遣垂及驍騎石越為前鋒，次於沔水。

translations.literal: Rui sent Chui and ferocious cavalry Shi Yue as vanguard, halting at the Mian River.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rui ordered Murong Chui and Shi Yue ahead to the Han River line.

sentences.zh: 垂、越夜命三軍人持十炬火，系炬於樹枝，光照十數里中。

translations.literal: Chui and Yue by night ordered the three hosts, each man holding ten torch fires, tying torches to tree branches so that light shone across ten or more li.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui and Shi Yue lit thousands of decoy fires in the trees, lighting the riverbank for miles.

sentences.zh: 沖懼，退還上明。

translations.literal: Chong was afraid and withdrew to Shangming.
translations.idiomatic: Faced with that display, Huan Chong pulled back to Shangming.

sentences.zh: 張蠔出斜谷，楊亮亦引兵退歸。

translations.literal: Zhang He emerged from Xie Valley; Yang Liang also led troops and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He advanced through Xie Valley until Yang Liang likewise retreated.

sentences.zh: 堅下書悉發諸州公私馬，人十丁遣一兵。

translations.literal: Jian issued a writ summoning all the provinces' public and private horses; for every ten adult males one soldier was dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Jian drafted every tenth able man and requisitioned horses public and private across the provinces.

sentences.zh: 門在灼然者，為崇文義從。

translations.literal: Those households whose exemption status was manifestly clear were enrolled as retainers who exalt culture and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Families plainly exempt from ordinary service were mustered into a literati volunteer corps.

sentences.zh: 良家子年二十已下，武藝驍勇，富室材雄者，皆拜羽林郎。

translations.literal: For sons of good families under twenty who were martially brave and from rich, heroic households, all were appointed gentlemen of the feathered forest.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy youths under twenty who excelled at arms became imperial guardsmen of the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 下書期克捷之日，以帝為尚書左僕射，謝安為吏部尚書，桓沖為侍中，並立第以待之。

translations.literal: He issued a writ setting the day of certain victory: he would make the emperor grand supervisor of the masters of writing, Xie An director of personnel, Huan Chong palace attendant, and would erect mansions awaiting them.
translations.idiomatic: He boasted that he would house Sima Yao, Xie An, and Huan Chong in ready-built mansions as his ministers after victory.

sentences.zh: 良家子至者三萬餘騎。

translations.literal: Sons of good families who arrived numbered more than thirty thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty thousand elite young horsemen reported for duty.

sentences.zh: 其秦州主簿金城趙盛之為建威將軍、少年都統。

translations.literal: Their Qinzhou clerk Zhao Sheng of Jincheng was appointed general who displays might and commander-in-chief of the youths.
translations.idiomatic: He named Zhao Sheng of Jincheng, a Qinzhou clerk, to lead these young recruits.

sentences.zh: 遣征南苻融、驃騎張蠔、撫軍苻方、衛軍梁成、平南慕容暐、冠軍慕容垂率步騎二十五萬為前鋒。

translations.literal: He dispatched southern expedition Fu Rong, chariot-and-horse Zhang He, military overseer Fu Fang, guards general Liang Cheng, southern pacifier Murong Wei, champion Murong Chui to lead two hundred fifty thousand foot and horse as the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: The first wave—Fu Rong, Zhang He, Fu Fang, Liang Cheng, Murong Wei, Murong Chui—took a quarter million men toward the front.

sentences.zh: 堅發長安，戎卒六十餘萬，騎二十七萬，前後千里，旗鼓相望。

translations.literal: Jian set out from Chang'an: armed soldiers more than six hundred thousand, cavalry two hundred seventy thousand, stretching a thousand li front to rear with drums and banners in sight of one another.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian himself left Chang'an he brought over six hundred thousand foot and two hundred seventy thousand horse in a column that spanned a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 堅至項城，涼州之兵始達咸陽，蜀漢之軍順流而下，幽、冀之眾至於彭城，東西萬里，水陸齊進。

translations.literal: When Jian reached Xiangcheng, Liangzhou's troops had only then reached Xianyang, Shu-Han's armies went downstream with the current, You and Ji hosts reached Pengcheng—ten thousand li from east to west, advancing together by water and land.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Jian reached Xiangcheng, Liangzhou contingents were still straggling into Xianyang, Sichuan fleets were sliding downriver, and Hebei divisions had reached Pengcheng—Qin's hosts stretched ten thousand li in a coordinated land-and-water advance.

sentences.zh: 運漕萬艘，自河入石門，達於汝、潁。

translations.literal: Transport barges numbered in the myriad; from the Yellow River they entered Stone Gate and reached the Ru and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand grain barges passed through Stone Gate from the Yellow River into the Ru-Ying network.

sentences.zh: 融等攻陷壽春，執晉平虜將軍徐元喜、安豐太守王先。

translations.literal: Rong and the others stormed and took Shouchun, capturing Jin's general who pacifies captives Xu Yuanxi and prefect of Anfeng Wang Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong's van took Shouyang, seizing Jin generals Xu Yuanxi and the Anfeng prefect Wang Xian.

sentences.zh: 垂攻陷鄖城，害晉將軍王太丘。

translations.literal: Chui stormed and took Yuncheng and killed Jin general Wang Taiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui seized Yuncheng and killed the Jin commander Wang Taiqiu.

sentences.zh: 梁成與其揚州刺史王顯、弋陽太守王詠等率眾五萬，屯於洛澗，柵淮以遏東軍。

translations.literal: Liang Cheng together with his inspector of Yangzhou Wang Xian, prefect of Yiyang Wang Yong, and others led a host of fifty thousand, encamped at the Luo Stream, palisaded the Huai to block the eastern army.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Cheng, Wang Xian, Wang Yong, and fifty thousand men walled the Huai at the Luo inlet to stop the eastern Jin relief force.

sentences.zh: 成頻敗王師。

translations.literal: Cheng repeatedly defeated the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Cheng repulsed several Jin attacks.

sentences.zh: 晉遣都督謝石、徐州刺史謝玄、豫州刺史桓伊、輔國謝琰等水陸七萬，相繼距融，去洛澗二十五里，憚成不進。

translations.literal: Jin sent area commander-in-chief Xie Shi, inspector of Xuzhou Xie Xuan, inspector of Yuzhou Huan Yi, general who aids the state Xie Yan, and others—seventy thousand by water and land—successively opposing Rong, twenty-five li from the Luo Stream, but feared Cheng and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shi, Xie Xuan, Huan Yi, and Xie Yan brought seventy thousand men to face Fu Rong but halted twenty-five li short of the Luo lines, intimidated by Liang Cheng.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍胡彬先保硤石，為融所逼，糧盡，詐揚沙以示融軍，潛遣使告石等曰：「今賊盛糧盡，恐不見大軍。

translations.literal: Dragon-prancing general Hu Bin first held Xiaoshi, was pressed by Rong, ran out of grain, feigned raising dust to show Rong's army, and secretly sent a messenger to tell Shi and others, "Now the bandits are strong and our grain is gone; I fear I will not see the great host."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Bin, trapped at Xiaoshi with empty granaries, kicked up dust as a bluff while secretly warning Xie Shi that Qin seemed overwhelming and supplies were gone.

sentences.zh: 」融軍人獲而送之。

translations.literal: " Rong's army captured him and sent him on.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong's men intercepted the courier and forwarded him to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 融乃馳使白堅曰：「賊少易俘，但懼其越逸，宜速進眾軍，掎禽賊帥。

translations.literal: Rong thereupon galloped a messenger to report to Jian, "The bandits are few and easy to capture, but I fear they will slip away; You should quickly advance the mass of armies to join in seizing the bandit commanders."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong sent urgent word that Jin was weak and ripe for netting if the main army hurried south.

sentences.zh: 」堅大悅，恐石等遁也，舍大軍于項城，以輕騎八千兼道赴之，令軍人曰：「敢言吾至壽春者拔舌。

translations.literal: " Jian was greatly pleased, feared that Shi and the others would flee, left the great army at Xiangcheng, and with eight thousand light cavalry pressed on by double marches, ordering the troops, "Whoever dares say We have reached Shouchun shall have his tongue pulled out."
translations.idiomatic: Elated, Jian abandoned the main host at Xiangcheng, raced ahead with eight thousand horse, and threatened anyone who revealed his arrival at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 」故石等弗知。

translations.literal: Therefore Shi and the others did not know.
translations.idiomatic: His secrecy kept the Jin command ignorant of his presence.

sentences.zh: 晉龍驤將軍劉牢之率勁卒五千，夜襲梁成壘，克之，斬成及王顯、王詠等十將，士卒死者萬五千。

translations.literal: Jin dragon-prancing general Liu Laizhi led five thousand crack troops, by night raided Liang Cheng's camp, took it, beheaded Cheng and Wang Xian, Wang Yong, and ten other generals; fifteen thousand soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laizhi's night raid on Liang Cheng's camp killed the Qin general and fifteen thousand men.

sentences.zh: 謝石等以既敗梁成，水陸繼進。

translations.literal: Xie Shi and the others, because they had already defeated Liang Cheng, advanced continuously by water and land.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened by Liu Laizhi's victory, the Jin army pushed forward on every axis.

sentences.zh: 堅與苻融登城而望王師，見部陣齊整，將士精銳，又北望八公山上草木，皆類人形，顧謂融曰：「此亦勍敵也，何謂少乎！

translations.literal: Jian together with Fu Rong ascended the wall and gazed on the royal army, saw the formations neat, generals and soldiers keen, and also looked north at the trees and grass on Mount Bagong—all resembling human shapes—turned and said to Rong, "These too are strong foes—how can you call them few!"
translations.idiomatic: From the wall Fu Jian and Fu Rong saw Jin's crisp ranks—and every bush on Bagong seemed a soldier—whereupon Jian muttered that this was no weak enemy.

sentences.zh: 」憮然有懼色。

translations.literal: He looked dismayed and showed fear.
translations.idiomatic: His face fell and fear showed plain.

sentences.zh: 初，朝廷聞堅入寇，會稽王道子以威儀鼓吹求助於鐘山之神，奉以相國之號。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the court heard that Jian was invading, Prince of Kuaiji Sima Daozi, with full honors and martial music, sought aid from the god of Mount Zhongshan and invested him with the title of minister of state.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as Qin marched south, Sima Daozi had implored Mount Zhong's deity with full ritual pomp, elevating it to ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 及堅之見草木狀人，若有力焉。

translations.literal: When Jian saw the grass and trees in human shape, it was as if there were power in it.
translations.idiomatic: The historian adds that the omen Jian read in the hillside scrub matched that divine appeal.

sentences.zh: 堅遣其尚書硃序說石等以眾盛，欲脅而降之。

translations.literal: Jian sent his director of the secretariat Zhu Xu to persuade Shi and the others with [Qin's] host's strength, wishing to coerce them into surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Jian ordered the captured Jin minister Zhu Xu to intimidate Xie Shi into capitulation.

sentences.zh: 序詭謂石曰：「若秦百萬之眾皆至，則莫可敵也。

translations.literal: Xu secretly said to Shi, "If all of Qin's million come, then none can withstand them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xu quietly warned that a united million-man host would be unstoppable,

sentences.zh: 及其眾軍未集，宜在速戰。

translations.literal: While their mass of armies is not yet gathered, you should fight a swift battle.
translations.idiomatic: but while Qin's columns were still scattered, Jin had to strike fast.

sentences.zh: 若挫其前鋒，可以得志。

translations.literal: If you break their vanguard, you can achieve your aim."
translations.idiomatic: Crush the spearhead, he urged, and the invasion would falter.

sentences.zh: 」石聞堅在壽春也，懼，謀不戰以疲之。

translations.literal: " When Shi heard that Jian was at Shouchun, he was afraid and planned not to fight in order to wear them down.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Fu Jian himself had reached Shouyang, Xie Shi hesitated to offer battle and hoped to delay.

sentences.zh: 謝琰勸從序言，遣使請戰，許之。

translations.literal: Xie Yan urged following Xu's words; they sent a messenger requesting battle, and [Jian] granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yan pressed him to trust Zhu Xu's advice; they challenged Fu Rong, who accepted.

sentences.zh: 時張蠔敗謝石于肥南，謝玄、謝琰勒卒數萬，陣以待之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang He had defeated Xie Shi south of Fei; Xie Xuan and Xie Yan led several tens of thousands of troops and drew up ranks to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He had just mauled Xie Shi south of the Fei River, so Xie Xuan and Xie Yan formed a battle line to meet him.

sentences.zh: 蠔乃退，列陣逼肥水。

translations.literal: He thereupon withdrew, arrayed his ranks pressing the Fei River.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He pulled back and anchored his formation tight against the Fei's north bank.

sentences.zh: 王師不得渡，遣使謂融曰：「君懸軍深入，置陣逼水，此持久之計，豈欲戰者乎？

translations.literal: The royal army could not cross and sent a messenger to say to Rong, "You hang your army deep in enemy territory, set your formation pressing the water—this is a plan for endurance; is it the intention of one who wishes to fight?
translations.idiomatic: Jin envoys told Fu Rong that a water's-edge stalemate suited Qin, not pitched battle,

sentences.zh: 若小退師，令將士周旋，僕與君公緩轡而觀之，不亦美乎！

translations.literal: If you slightly withdraw your troops and let generals and soldiers maneuver, your servant and you, my lord, may slacken the reins and watch—is not this beautiful!"
translations.idiomatic: and proposed a minor Qin pullback so both sides could maneuver—an offer meant to tempt him.

sentences.zh: 」融於是麾軍卻陣，欲因其濟水，覆而取之。

translations.literal: " Rong thereupon signaled the army to pull back the formation, wishing to take advantage of their crossing the water to overturn and capture them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong ordered a feigned retreat, planning to crush Jin mid-river.

sentences.zh: 軍遂奔退，制之不可止。

translations.literal: The army thereupon ran in flight; he could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Instead the line collapsed into a rout he could not halt.

sentences.zh: 融馳騎略陣，馬倒被殺，軍遂大敗。

translations.literal: Rong galloped his horse along the ranks, his horse fell, and he was killed; the army thereupon suffered great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong fell from his horse under Jin arrows, and his host shattered.

sentences.zh: 王師乘勝追擊，至於青岡，死者相枕。

translations.literal: The royal army exploited victory in pursuit as far as Qinggang; the dead lay pillow to pillow.
translations.idiomatic: Jin pursuers drove the fugitives to Qinggang, where corpses piled deep.

sentences.zh: 堅為流矢所中，單騎遁還於淮北，饑甚，人有進壺飧豚髀者，堅食之，大悅，曰：「昔公孫豆粥何以加也！

translations.literal: Jian was struck by a stray arrow, fled alone on horseback to north of the Huai, was extremely hungry; someone offered a pot of cooked food and a pig thigh—Jian ate it and was greatly pleased, saying, "How can Gongsun's bean gruel add to this!"
translations.idiomatic: A wounded Fu Jian fled north of the Huai, starving until a commoner fed him stew and pork; he compared the meal to the gruel once offered to Emperor Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 」使賜帛十匹，綿十斤。

translations.literal: " He ordered ten bolts of silk and ten jin of floss bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to reward the peasant with silk and cotton.

sentences.zh: 辭曰：「臣聞白龍厭天池之樂而見困豫且，陛下目所睹也，耳所聞也。

translations.literal: He declined, saying, "Your subject has heard that the white dragon tired of the joy of the heavenly pool and was trapped by Yu Ju—what Your Majesty's eyes have seen and ears have heard.
translations.idiomatic: The man refused, citing the fable of the white dragon who left paradise only to be caught by a fisherman,

sentences.zh: 今蒙塵之難，豈自天乎！

translations.literal: Now the hardship of enduring dust—is it from Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: and asked whether Jian's downfall was truly Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 且妄施不為惠，妄受不為忠。

translations.literal: Moreover reckless giving is not kindness, reckless accepting is not loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Unmerited gifts, he said, were no kindness, nor was accepting them loyalty.

sentences.zh: 陛下，臣之父母也，安有子養而求報哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty is your subject's father and mother—how can a son who is nourished seek reward!"
translations.idiomatic: A child owed parents care without thought of payback.

sentences.zh: 」弗顧而退。

translations.literal: " He paid no heed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed off despite Jian's command.

sentences.zh: 堅大慚，顧謂其夫人張氏曰：「朕若用朝臣之言，豈見今日之事邪！

translations.literal: Jian was greatly ashamed, turned and said to his lady Zhang, "If We had used the court ministers' words, how could We have seen today's affair!
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Jian told Empress Zhang that he should have listened to his advisers,

sentences.zh: 當何面目復臨天下乎？

translations.literal: With what face shall We again face all under Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: and wondered how he could ever show himself to the realm.

sentences.zh: 」潸然流涕而去。

translations.literal: " Weeping streaming tears, he departed.
translations.idiomatic: He left in tears.

sentences.zh: 聞風聲鶴唳，皆謂晉師之至。

translations.literal: Hearing wind sounds and crane cries, all said the Jin army had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Every gust and birdcall seemed to the fugitives like pursuing Jin troops.

sentences.zh: 其僕射張天錫、尚書硃序及徐元喜等皆歸順。

translations.literal: Their vice-director Zhang Tianxi, director Zhu Xu, and Xu Yuanxi and others all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi, Zhu Xu, Xu Yuanxi, and other Qin notables surrendered to Jin.

sentences.zh: 初，諺言「堅不出項」，群臣勸堅停項，為六軍聲鎮，堅不從，故敗。

translations.literal: Earlier a proverb said, "Jian will not leave Xiang"; the host of ministers urged Jian to halt at Xiang and be the six armies' stabilizing voice, but Jian did not follow—therefore he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Folk wisdom had warned Fu Jian not to advance past Xiangcheng; ministers begged him to stop there and command from the rear, but his rashness brought defeat.

sentences.zh: 諸軍悉潰，惟慕容垂一軍獨全，堅以千餘騎赴之。

translations.literal: All hosts entirely broke; only Murong Chui's one army alone remained intact; Jian went to him with more than a thousand cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Every column dissolved except Murong Chui's, so Jian rode to his camp with a thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 垂子寶勸垂殺堅，垂不從，乃以兵屬堅。

translations.literal: Chui's son Bao urged Chui to kill Jian; Chui did not follow, and thereupon placed his troops under Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao urged patricide, but Chui refused and instead lent his intact division to shield Jian.

sentences.zh: 初，慕容暐屯鄖城，姜成等守漳口，晉隨郡太守夏侯澄攻姜成，斬之，暐棄其眾奔還。

translations.literal: Earlier Murong Wei had been encamped at Yuncheng; Jiang Cheng and others guarded the Zhang ford; Jin's prefect of Sui commandery Xiahou Cheng attacked Jiang Cheng, beheaded him, and Wei abandoned his host and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Murong Wei had garrisoned Yuncheng until Jin's Xiahou Cheng killed his defender Jiang Cheng at the Zhang crossing, forcing Wei to bolt.

sentences.zh: 堅收離集散，比至洛陽，眾十餘萬，百官威儀軍容粗備。

translations.literal: Jian gathered the scattered and collected the dispersed; by the time he reached Luoyang, the host was more than one hundred thousand, and the hundred officials' honors and military appearance were roughly complete.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian scraped together stragglers until, by Luoyang, he again commanded over a hundred thousand men with something like a court and escort.

sentences.zh: 未及關而垂有貳志，說堅請巡撫燕、岱，並求拜墓，堅許之。

translations.literal: Before he reached the passes Chui harbored a second mind; he persuaded Jian to request a tour to pacify Yan and Dai and also to ask leave to sweep his ancestors' tombs, and Jian granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Before the capital gates Murong Chui begged leave to pacify the old Yan homeland and tend clan graves; Jian consented.

sentences.zh: 權翼固諫以為不可，堅不從。

translations.literal: Quan Yi firmly remonstrated, holding it impermissible; Jian did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yi warned that releasing Chui was fatal; Jian ignored him.

sentences.zh: 尋懼垂為變，悔之，遣驍騎石越率卒三千戍鄴，驃騎張蠔率羽林五千戍并州，留兵四千配鎮軍毛當戍洛陽。

translations.literal: Soon he feared Chui would rebel, regretted it, sent ferocious cavalry Shi Yue leading three thousand troops to garrison Ye, chariot-and-horse Zhang He leading five thousand feather-forest guards to garrison Bingzhou, and left four thousand troops assigned to general who garrisons Mao Dang to garrison Luoyang.
