translations.idiomatic: Second thoughts led him to garrison Ye, Bingzhou, and Luoyang against Murong Chui's return.

sentences.zh: 堅至自淮南，次於長安東之行宮，哭苻融而後入，告罪於其太廟，赦殊死已下，文武增位一級，厲兵課農，存恤孤老，諸士卒不返者皆復其家終世。

translations.literal: Jian arrived from Huainan, halted at the traveling palace east of Chang'an, wept for Fu Rong and afterward entered, announced his fault at the grand ancestral temple, pardoned all short of capital crimes, raised civil and military ranks one grade, hardened troops and assessed farming, cared for orphans and aged, and for all soldiers who did not return restored their families exempt for life.
translations.idiomatic: Back near Chang'an he mourned Fu Rong, confessed before the ancestors, issued amnesties and relief, and exempted the households of the fallen forever.

sentences.zh: 贈融大司馬，諡曰哀公。

translations.literal: He posthumously awarded Rong grand marshal with posthumous title Duke Ai.
translations.idiomatic: He ennobled the dead Fu Rong as grand marshal and posthumously titled him Duke of Lament.

sentences.zh: 衛軍從事中郎丁零、翟斌反于河南，長樂公苻丕遣慕容垂及苻飛龍討之。

translations.literal: Adjutant under the guards general Zhai Bin of the Dingling rebelled south of the Yellow River; Duke of Changle Fu Pi sent Murong Chui and Fu Feilong to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: When Dingling leader Zhai Bin rose south of the river, Fu Pi ordered Murong Chui and Fu Feilong against him.

sentences.zh: 垂南結丁零，殺飛龍，盡坑其眾。

translations.literal: Chui allied south with the Dingling, killed Feilong, and buried his host in pits.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui slew Fu Feilong, allied with Zhai Bin, and annihilated the Di escort.

sentences.zh: 豫州牧、平原公苻暉遣毛當擊翟斌，為斌所敗，當死之。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yuzhou, Duke of Pingyuan Fu Hui, sent Mao Dang to strike Zhai Bin; he was defeated by Bin and Dang died in it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hui's column under Mao Dang lost to Zhai Bin; Mao Dang fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 垂子農亡奔列人，招集群盜，眾至萬數千。

translations.literal: Chui's son Nong fled to Lieren, summoned bandit gangs, and the host reached several myriads.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Nong fled to Lieren, rallied outlaws, and raised tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 丕遣石越擊之，為農所敗，越死之。

translations.literal: Pi sent Shi Yue to strike him; he was defeated by Nong and Yue died in it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi's general Shi Yue died attacking Murong Nong.

sentences.zh: 垂引丁零、烏丸之眾二十餘萬，為飛梯地道以攻鄴城。

translations.literal: Chui led more than two hundred thousand of Dingling and Wuhuan hosts, made flying ladders and tunnel ways, and attacked Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui besieged Ye with two hundred thousand Dingling and Wuhuan auxiliaries, using siege ladders and saps.

sentences.zh: 慕容暐弟燕故濟北王泓先為北地長史，聞垂攻鄴，亡命奔關東，收諸馬牧鮮卑，眾至數千，還屯華陰。

translations.literal: Murong Wei's younger brother, Yan's former prince of Jibei, Hong, had been chief clerk of Beidi; hearing Chui attack Ye, he fled for his life east of the pass, gathered the horse-pasture Xianbei, reached several thousand, and returned to encamp at Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hong, former prince of Jibei, fled east, rallied Xianbei herders, and seized Huayin with thousands of riders.

sentences.zh: 慕容暐乃潛使諸弟及宗人起兵於外。

translations.literal: Murong Wei thereupon secretly ordered younger brothers and clansmen to raise troops outside.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Wei smuggled word for kinsmen to rise beyond the capital.

sentences.zh: 堅遣將軍強永率騎擊之，為泓所敗，泓眾遂盛，自稱使持節、大都督陝西諸軍事、大將軍、雍州牧、濟北王，推叔父垂為丞相、都督陝東諸軍事、領大司馬、冀州牧、吳王。

translations.literal: Jian sent general Qiang Yong leading cavalry to strike him; he was defeated by Hong, and Hong's host thereupon grew strong; he styled himself commissioner with extraordinary powers, grand commander-in-chief of military affairs in Shaanxi, grand general, shepherd of Yongzhou, prince of Jibei, and promoted his uncle Chui as chancellor, grand commander-in-chief of military affairs east of Shan, concurrent grand marshal, shepherd of Jizhou, prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Yong lost to Murong Hong, who then proclaimed himself prince of Jibei with grand titles and named Murong Chui his chancellor in the east.

sentences.zh: 堅謂權翼曰：「吾不從卿言，鮮卑至是。

translations.literal: Jian said to Quan Yi, "We did not follow your words—the Xianbei have reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: Jian told Quan Yi that ignoring his warning had unleashed the Murongs.

sentences.zh: 關東之地，吾不復與之爭，將若泓何？

translations.literal: The lands east of the pass—We will not again contest them with them; what shall We do about Hong?"
translations.idiomatic: He conceded Shandong but asked how to stop Murong Hong.

sentences.zh: 」翼曰：「寇不可長。

translations.literal: " Yi said, "Banditry must not be allowed to grow.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yi replied that rebellion must be crushed early,

sentences.zh: 慕容垂正可據山東為亂，不暇近逼。

translations.literal: Murong Chui may only occupy Shandong and make trouble, without leisure to press near.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui was busy in Shandong and no immediate threat to Guanzhong,

sentences.zh: 今暐及宗族種類盡在京師，鮮卑之眾布於畿甸，實社稷之元憂，宜遣重將討之。

translations.literal: Now Wei and the whole clan and kind are all in the capital; Xianbei hosts are spread through the capital region—they are truly the fundamental worry for the altars of soil and grain; You should dispatch a weighty general to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: but Murong Wei and every Xianbei noble still in Chang'an posed the graver danger.

sentences.zh: 」堅乃以廣平公苻熙為使持節、都督雍州雜戎諸軍事、鎮東大將軍、雍州刺史，鎮蒲阪。

translations.literal: " Jian thereupon made Duke of Guangping Fu Xi commissioner with extraordinary powers, area commander-in-chief of miscellaneous Rong affairs in Yongzhou, general who garrisons the east, inspector of Yongzhou, and stationed him at Puban.
translations.idiomatic: He named Fu Xi to hold Puban against western thrusts,

sentences.zh: 征苻睿為都督中外諸軍事、衛大將軍、司隸校尉、錄尚書事，配兵五萬以左將軍竇沖為長史，龍驤姚萇為司馬，討泓于華澤。

translations.literal: Called Fu Rui area commander-in-chief of all military affairs within and without, guards grand marshal, colonel director of retainer, concurrent recorder of affairs with the secretariat, assigned him fifty thousand troops with left general Dou Chong as chief clerk and dragon-prancing Yao Chang as marshal, to campaign against Hong at Huaze.
translations.idiomatic: and Fu Rui with Yao Chang and fifty thousand men to destroy Murong Hong at Huaze.

sentences.zh: 平陽太守慕容沖起兵河東，有眾二萬，進攻蒲阪，堅命竇沖討之。

translations.literal: Murong Chong, prefect of Pingyang, raised troops in Hedong, had a host of twenty thousand, advanced to attack Puban, and Jian ordered Dou Chong to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong rose in Hedong with twenty thousand men and struck Puban until Jian sent Dou Chong.

sentences.zh: 苻睿勇果輕敵，不恤士眾。

translations.literal: Fu Rui was brave and decisive, treated the enemy lightly, and did not pity soldiers and hosts.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rui was rash, despised his foe, and wasted lives.

sentences.zh: 泓聞其至也，懼，率眾將奔關東，睿馳兵要之。

translations.literal: When Hong heard he had come, he was afraid and led the host planning to flee east of the pass; Rui galloped troops to intercept him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hong tried to bolt east; Fu Rui raced to cut him off.

sentences.zh: 姚萇諫曰：「鮮卑有思歸之心，宜驅令出關，不可遏也。

translations.literal: Yao Chang remonstrated, "The Xianbei have hearts that yearn to return home; you ought to drive them out of the pass, not block them."
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang urged letting homesick Xianbei leave the pass rather than forcing a fight.

sentences.zh: 」睿弗從，戰于華澤，睿敗績，被殺。

translations.literal: " Rui did not follow; they fought at Huaze; Rui's lines were broken and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rui ignored him, fought at Huaze, and died in defeat.

sentences.zh: 堅大怒。

translations.literal: Jian was greatly angry.
translations.idiomatic: Jian exploded with rage.

sentences.zh: 萇懼誅，遂叛。

translations.literal: Chang feared execution and thereupon rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing blame, Yao Chang mutinied.

sentences.zh: 竇衝擊慕容沖於河東，大破之，沖率騎八千奔於泓軍。

translations.literal: Dou Chong struck Murong Chong in Hedong, greatly defeated him, and Chong led eight thousand cavalry to flee to Hong's army.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chong routed Murong Chong, who fled with eight thousand horse to Murong Hong.

sentences.zh: 泓眾至十餘萬，遣使謂堅曰：「秦為無道，滅我社稷。

translations.literal: Hong's host reached more than one hundred thousand; he sent a messenger to tell Jian, "Qin acted without the Way and destroyed our altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hong's army swelled past a hundred thousand; he wrote that Qin had extinguished Yan without justice,

sentences.zh: 今天誘其衷，使秦師傾敗，將欲興復大燕。

translations.literal: Now Heaven has opened their bosom and made Qin's army overturn in defeat; We wish to raise Great Yan anew.
translations.idiomatic: and that Heaven's vengeance invited the Murongs to restore Yan.

sentences.zh: 吳王已定關東，可速資備大駕，奉送家兄皇帝並宗室功臣之家。

translations.literal: The prince of Wu has already settled Shandong; You can quickly supply and equip the great carriages and escort home your elder brother the emperor together with the houses of meritorious ministers of the clan.
translations.idiomatic: He demanded carriages to escort Murong Wei and noble hostages east,

sentences.zh: 泓當率關中燕人，翼衛皇帝，還返鄴都，與秦以武牢為界，分王天下，永為鄰好，不復為秦之患也。

translations.literal: Hong will lead the Yan people of Guanzhong to wing and guard the emperor and return to Ye, share kingship with Qin with Martial Stronghold as boundary, be neighboring friends forever, and no longer be Qin's worry."
translations.idiomatic: promising to shepherd former Yan subjects home and divide the realm at Hulao pass.

sentences.zh: 钜鹿公輕戇銳進，為亂兵所害，非泓之意。

translations.literal: The duke of Julu's rash impetuosity and sharp advance caused him to be killed by mutinous troops—it was not Hong's intent.
translations.idiomatic: He disclaimed responsibility for Fu Rui's death in the melee.

sentences.zh: 」堅大怒，召慕容暐責之曰：「卿父子幹紀僭亂，乖逆人神，朕應天行神，盡兵勢而得卿。

translations.literal: " Jian was greatly angry, summoned Murong Wei, and rebuked him, saying, "You father and son violated the law, usurped and rebelled, opposed Heaven and man; We responded to Heaven and exercised spirit, exhausted military force and obtained you.
translations.idiomatic: Jian summoned Murong Wei, accusing the Murongs of treason despite his mercy,

sentences.zh: 卿非改迷歸善，而合宗蒙宥，兄弟布列上將、納言，雖曰破滅，其實若歸。

translations.literal: You did not reform error and return to good, yet the whole clan received forgiveness; brothers were arrayed as senior generals and intake advisers—though it was called destruction, in truth it was like returning home.
translations.idiomatic: noting how generously he had employed the captives,

sentences.zh: 奈何因王師小敗，便猖悖若此！

translations.literal: How can you, because the royal army suffered a small defeat, act so wildly rebellious!
translations.idiomatic: and raged that a single setback should not license revolt.

sentences.zh: 垂為長蛇於關東，泓、沖稱兵內侮。

translations.literal: Chui is a long snake east of the pass; Hong and Chong raise arms and insult within.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui strangled the east while Hong and Murong Chong struck inside Guanzhong,

sentences.zh: 泓書如此，卿欲去者，朕當相資。

translations.literal: Hong's letter is thus; if you wish to go, We shall supply you.
translations.idiomatic: and said he would fund their departure if they wished to leave.

sentences.zh: 卿之宗族，可謂人面獸心，殆不可以國士期也。

translations.literal: Your clan may be called human faces with beast hearts—truly they cannot be expected to behave as men of the state!"
translations.idiomatic: He called the Murongs beasts in human masks.

sentences.zh: 」暐叩頭流血，泣涕陳謝。

translations.literal: " Wei knocked his head until it bled, weeping tears and stating his apology.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Wei kowtowed in terror and tears.

sentences.zh: 堅久之曰：「《書》云，父子兄弟無相及也。

translations.literal: Jian, after a long time, said, "The Book says: father and son, elder and younger brothers do not reach one another with punishment.
translations.idiomatic: After a long silence Jian quoted the Shangshu on punishing individuals, not kin,

sentences.zh: 卿之忠誠，實簡朕心，此自三豎之罪，非卿之過。

translations.literal: Your loyalty truly reaches Our heart; this is the crime of the three villains themselves, not your fault.
translations.idiomatic: and blamed only the three Murong ringleaders,

sentences.zh: 」復其位而待之如初。

translations.literal: " He restored his rank and treated him as at first.
translations.idiomatic: then restored Murong Wei's titles.

sentences.zh: 命暐以書招喻垂及泓、沖，使息兵還長安，恕其反叛之咎。

translations.literal: He ordered Wei to write summoning Chui and Hong and Chong to cease arms and return to Chang'an, forgiving their crime of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He made Murong Wei write ordering the rebels to disarm and return under amnesty,

sentences.zh: 而暐密遣使者謂泓曰：「今秦數已終，長安怪異特甚，當不復能久立。

translations.literal: But Wei secretly sent envoys to tell Hong, "Now Qin's reckoning is ended; Chang'an's prodigies are especially extreme—it cannot long stand.
translations.idiomatic: yet secretly told Murong Hong that Qin's omens foretold collapse,

sentences.zh: 吾既籠中之人，必無還理。

translations.literal: We, already a man in a cage, certainly have no prospect of return.
translations.idiomatic: confessed that he himself was trapped beyond rescue,

sentences.zh: 昔不能保守宗廟，致令傾喪若斯，吾罪人也，不足復顧吾之存亡。

translations.literal: In the past We could not preserve the ancestral temples and caused them to be overturned like this—We are a guilty man, not worth again caring about Our survival.
translations.idiomatic: and disclaimed personal survival,

sentences.zh: 社稷不輕，勉建大業，以興復為務。

translations.literal: The altars of soil and grain are not light—strive to build the great enterprise and make restoration your task.
translations.idiomatic: urging his kinsman to put dynastic revival first,

sentences.zh: 可以吳王為相國，中山王為太宰、領大司馬，汝可為大將軍、領司徒，承制封拜。

translations.literal: You may make the prince of Wu minister of state, the prince of Zhongshan grand steward and concurrent grand marshal; you may be grand general and concurrent director of education, invest and appoint by edict as circumstances warrant.
translations.idiomatic: laying out a shadow cabinet with Murong Chui as minister, Murong Chong as grand steward, and Murong Hong as commander,

sentences.zh: 聽吾死問，汝使即尊位。

translations.literal: When you hear of Our death, your envoy may at once assume the supreme position."
translations.idiomatic: and authorizing Hong to seize the throne on news of Wei's death.

sentences.zh: 」泓於是進向長安，改年曰燕興。

translations.literal: " Hong thereupon advanced toward Chang'an and changed the era name to Yanxing.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hong then marched on Chang'an and proclaimed a new reign title, Yanxing.

sentences.zh: 是時鬼夜哭，三旬而止。

translations.literal: At that time ghosts wept at night; after thirty days it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: For a month the capital was haunted by night wailing that then ceased.

sentences.zh: 堅率步騎二萬討姚萇於北地，次於趙氏塢，使護軍楊璧遊騎三千，斷其奔路，右軍徐成、左軍竇沖、鎮軍毛盛等屢戰敗之，仍斷其運水之路。

translations.literal: Jian led twenty thousand foot and horse to campaign against Yao Chang at Beidi, halted at Zhao's Stockade, ordered guards general Yang Bi with three thousand roaming cavalry to cut off his flight routes; right army Xu Cheng, left army Dou Chong, garrison general Mao Sheng and others repeatedly fought and defeated him, still cutting off his route for transporting water.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian camped at Zhao Stockade, sent Yang Bi's riders to cut Yao Chang's retreat, and used Xu Cheng, Dou Chong, and Mao Sheng to beat him repeatedly while blocking every water convoy.

sentences.zh: 馮翊遊欽因淮南之敗，聚眾數千，保據頻陽，遣軍運水及粟，以饋姚萇，楊璧盡獲之。

translations.literal: You Qin of Pingyi, because of the defeat south of the Huai, gathered several thousand, held Pin-yang, sent troops transporting water and millet to feed Yao Chang; Yang Bi captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: You Qin of Fanyi exploited Qin's southern disaster to supply Yao Chang from Pinyang until Yang Bi seized every convoy.

sentences.zh: 萇軍渴甚，遣其弟鎮北尹買率勁卒二萬決堰。

translations.literal: Chang's army was extremely thirsty; he sent his younger brother, general who garrisons the north Yinmai, leading twenty thousand crack troops to breach the weir.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang ordered his brother Yinmai with twenty thousand men to break the dam and reach water.

sentences.zh: 竇沖率眾敗其軍于鸛雀渠，斬尹買及首級萬三千。

translations.literal: Dou Chong led the host and defeated his army at the Guanque Channel, beheaded Yinmai and thirteen thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chong crushed them at Guanque Ditch, killing Yinmai and thirteen thousand.

sentences.zh: 萇眾危懼，人有渴死者。

translations.literal: Chang's host was in peril and fear; some men died of thirst.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang's men were parched and desperate; some died of thirst.

sentences.zh: 俄而降雨于萇營，營中水三尺，周營百步之外，寸餘而已，於是萇軍大振。

translations.literal: Shortly rain fell on Chang's camp—three chi of water in the camp, yet only a bit more than an inch beyond a hundred paces around the camp; thereupon Chang's army was greatly heartened.
translations.idiomatic: Then rain soaked only Yao Chang's camp ankle-deep while a ring just outside stayed dry—a miracle that revived his army.

sentences.zh: 堅方食，去案怒曰：「天其無心，何故降澤賊營！

translations.literal: Jian was just eating, pushed away the table in anger, and said, "Is Heaven without a heart—why does it send moisture to the bandit camp!
translations.idiomatic: At his meal Fu Jian flung his table aside, raging that Heaven would water the rebels,

sentences.zh: 」萇又東引慕容泓為援。

translations.literal: " Chang also drew Murong Hong east as reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: while Yao Chang linked up with Murong Hong.

sentences.zh: 泓謀臣高蓋、宿勤崇等以泓德望後沖，且持法苛峻，乃殺泓，立沖為皇太弟，承制行事，自相署置。

translations.literal: Hong's strategists Gao Gai, Suqin Chong, and others, because Hong's virtue and standing lagged behind Chong's and moreover his holding of the law was harsh and severe, thereupon killed Hong, established Chong as imperial heir younger brother, acted by edict, and appointed one another to posts.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gai and Suqin Chong murdered Murong Hong for his harsh rule and weaker charisma, elevated Murong Chong as heir-apparent regent, and handed out offices on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 姚萇留其弟征虜緒守楊渠川大營，率眾七萬來攻堅。

translations.literal: Yao Chang left his younger brother, general who punishes captives Xu, guarding the great camp at Yangqu Stream, led seventy thousand to attack Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang left Yao Xu at Yangqu and struck Chang'an with seventy thousand men.

sentences.zh: 堅遣楊璧等擊之，為萇所敗，獲楊璧、毛盛、徐成及前軍齊午等數十人，皆禮而遣之。

translations.literal: Jian sent Yang Bi and others to strike them; they were defeated by Chang, who captured Yang Bi, Mao Sheng, Xu Cheng, and forward army Qi Wu and several tens of others—all were treated with courtesy and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's counterattack failed; Yao Chang captured Yang Bi and other generals but courteously released them.

sentences.zh: 苻暉率洛陽、陝城之眾七萬歸於長安。

translations.literal: Fu Hui led seventy thousand from Luoyang and Shancheng and returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hui marched seventy thousand men from Luoyang and the Shan forts back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史王廣遣將軍王蠔率蜀漢之眾來赴難。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yizhou Wang Guang sent general Wang Hao leading Shu-Han hosts to come to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guang of Yizhou dispatched Wang Hao with Sichuan troops to relieve the throne.

sentences.zh: 堅聞慕容沖去長安二百餘里，引師而歸，使撫軍苻方戍驪山，拜苻暉使持節、散騎常侍、都督中外諸軍事、車騎大將軍、司隸校尉、錄尚書，配兵五萬距沖，河間公苻琳為中軍大將軍，為暉後繼。

translations.literal: Jian heard that Murong Chong was more than two hundred li from Chang'an, led the army back, ordered military overseer Fu Fang to garrison Mount Li, appointed Fu Hui commissioner with extraordinary powers, sanqi permanent attendant, area commander-in-chief of all military affairs within and without, general of chariots and cavalry, colonel director of retainer, concurrent recorder of affairs with the secretariat, assigned fifty thousand troops to oppose Chong, Duke of Hejian Fu Lin as grand general of the central army to follow Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Murong Chong neared Chang'an, Fu Jian rushed west, left Fu Fang on Lishan, and gave Fu Hui fifty thousand men to block Murong Chong while Fu Lin backed him with the central army.

sentences.zh: 沖乃令婦人乘牛馬為眾，揭竿為旗，揚土為塵，督厲其眾，晨攻暉營于鄭西。

translations.literal: Chong thereupon ordered women to ride oxen and horses as a host, raised poles as flags, tossed earth as dust, urged and hardened his host, and at dawn attacked Hui's camp west of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong used women, dust, and sham banners to mask a dawn assault on Fu Hui west of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 暉出距戰，沖揚塵鼓噪，暉師敗績。

translations.literal: Hui went out to oppose battle; Chong raised dust and drummed and shouted; Hui's army suffered rout.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hui rode out to meet him but Murong Chong's dust and noise broke his line.

sentences.zh: 堅又以尚書姜宇為前將軍，與苻琳率眾三萬，擊沖於灞上，為沖所敗，宇死之，琳中流矢，沖遂據阿房城。

translations.literal: Jian again made director of the secretariat Jiang Yu forward general; together with Fu Lin he led thirty thousand to strike Chong at Bashang, was defeated by Chong—Yu died in it, Lin was struck by a stray arrow, and Chong thereupon occupied Epang city.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian sent Jiang Yu and Fu Lin with thirty thousand to Bashang; Murong Chong killed Jiang Yu, wounded Fu Lin, and seized Epang.

sentences.zh: 初，堅之滅燕，沖姊為清河公主，年十四，有殊色，堅納之，寵冠後庭。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jian destroyed Yan, Chong's elder sister was princess of Qinghe, age fourteen, of extraordinary beauty; Jian took her in, and her favor topped the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin conquered Yan, Fu Jian took Murong Chong's fourteen-year-old sister, the Princess of Qinghe, as concubine and doted on her above all others.

sentences.zh: 沖年十二，亦有龍陽之姿，堅又幸之。

translations.literal: Chong, age twelve, also had the posture of Longyang; Jian also favored him.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve Murong Chong possessed the same androgynous allure, and Jian bedded him too.

sentences.zh: 姊弟專寵，宮人莫進。

translations.literal: The sister and brother monopolized favor; palace women could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The siblings shared the harem to the exclusion of every other woman.

sentences.zh: 長安歌之曰：「一雌復一雄，雙飛入紫宮。

translations.literal: Chang'an sang of them, saying, "One hen again one cock, pair-flying into the purple palace."
translations.idiomatic: Ballads mocked a hen and a rooster flying together into the purple palace.

sentences.zh: 」咸懼為亂。

translations.literal: All feared there would be disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The court feared scandal and revolt.

sentences.zh: 王猛切諫，堅乃出沖。

translations.literal: Wang Meng remonstrated sharply, and Jian thereupon sent Chong out.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng's blunt warning finally got Murong Chong expelled from the palace.

sentences.zh: 長安又謠曰：「鳳皇鳳皇止阿房。

translations.literal: Chang'an had another ditty: "Phoenix, phoenix, stop at Epang."
translations.idiomatic: A new rhyme said the phoenix would alight on Epang,

sentences.zh: 」堅以鳳皇非梧桐不棲，非竹實不食，乃植桐竹數十萬株于阿房城以待之。

translations.literal: " Jian held that the phoenix does not roost unless on paulownia, does not eat unless bamboo fruit; thereupon he planted several hundred thousand paulownia and bamboo at Epang city to await it.
translations.idiomatic: so Fu Jian planted bamboo and paulownia at Epang to lure the mythical bird.

sentences.zh: 沖小字鳳皇，至是，終為堅賊，入止阿房城焉。

translations.literal: Chong's childhood name was Phoenix; at this point he in the end became Jian's bandit, entered and stopped at Epang city.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong's pet name had been Phoenix; he now fulfilled the omen as Fu Jian's scourge by seizing Epang.

sentences.zh: 晉西中郎將桓石虔進據魯陽，遣河南太守高茂北戍洛陽。

translations.literal: Jin's western middle general Huan Shiqian advanced and held Luyang, sent Henan prefect Gao Mao to garrison Luoyang northward.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Shiqian seized Luyang and posted Gao Mao north of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 晉冠軍謝玄次於下邳，徐州刺史趙遷棄彭城奔還。

translations.literal: Jin champion Xie Xuan halted at Xiapi; inspector of Xuzhou Zhao Qian abandoned Pengcheng and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan camped at Xiapi while Qin's Zhao Qian fled Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 玄前鋒張願追遷及於碭山，轉戰而免。

translations.literal: Xuan's vanguard Zhang Yuan pursued Qian and caught him at Mount Dang, fought in circles and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuan chased Zhao Qian to Dangshan and fought him to a draw.

sentences.zh: 玄進據彭城。

translations.literal: Xuan advanced and held Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan then occupied Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 時呂光討平西域三十六國，所獲珍寶以萬萬計。

translations.literal: At that time Lu Guang had campaigned and pacified thirty-six states of the Western Regions; the precious goods captured were reckoned in myriads of myriads.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guang had subdued thirty-six Tarim kingdoms and seized treasure beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 堅下書以光為使持節、散騎常侍、都督玉門以西諸軍事、安西將軍、西域校尉，進封順鄉侯，增邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Jian issued a writ appointing Guang commissioner with extraordinary powers, sanqi permanent attendant, area commander-in-chief of military affairs west of Jade Gate, general who pacifies the west, colonel of the Western Regions, advanced enfeoffment to marquis of Shunxiang, increased fief by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian promoted Lu Guang with full western commands and a larger fief.

sentences.zh: 劉牢之伐兗州，堅刺史張崇棄鄄城奔于慕容垂。

translations.literal: Liu Laizhi campaigned against Yanzhou; Jian's inspector Zhang Chong abandoned Juancheng and fled to Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laizhi struck Yanzhou; Zhang Chong abandoned Juancheng for Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 牢之遣將軍劉襲追崇，戰于河南，斬其東平太守楊光而退。

translations.literal: Laizhi sent general Liu Xi pursuing Chong, fought south of the Yellow River, beheaded his prefect of Dongping Yang Guang, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xi killed Qin's Dongping prefect south of the river and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 牢之遂據鄄城。

translations.literal: Laizhi thereupon held Juancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laizhi then held Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 慕容沖進逼長安，堅登城觀之，歎曰：「此虜何從出也？

translations.literal: Murong Chong pressed Chang'an; Jian ascended the wall and watched them, sighed, saying, "Whence come these bandits?
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong closed on Chang'an; Fu Jian from the wall marveled at the size of the host,

sentences.zh: 其強若斯！

translations.literal: Their strength is like this!"
translations.idiomatic: astonished at their strength.

sentences.zh: 」大言責沖曰：「爾輩群奴正可牧牛羊，何為送死！

translations.literal: " He shouted loudly, rebuking Chong, saying, "You pack of slaves are fit only to herd oxen and sheep—why come to deliver death!
translations.idiomatic: He bellowed insults, calling them slave herders fit only for livestock,

sentences.zh: 」沖曰：「奴則奴矣，既厭奴苦，復欲取爾見代。

translations.literal: " Chong said, "Slave is slave—having tired of the bitterness of slavery, We again wish to take you and replace you.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong retorted that slaves who had endured slavery meant to replace their masters,

sentences.zh: 」堅遣使送錦袍一領遺沖，稱詔曰：「古人兵交，使在其間。

translations.literal: " Jian sent an envoy presenting Chong one lined brocade robe, stating by edict, "When men of old crossed arms, envoys went between them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian sent a silk robe with a message citing ancient courtesy between enemies,

sentences.zh: 卿遠來草創，得無勞乎？

translations.literal: You have come far in rough founding—can it be without toil?
translations.idiomatic: asking whether the campaign had worn him out,

sentences.zh: 今送一袍，以明本懷。

translations.literal: Now We send one robe to clarify Our original mind.
translations.idiomatic: offering the gift as a token of past kindness,

sentences.zh: 朕於卿恩分如何，而於一朝忽為此變！

translations.literal: What have been Our kindness and portion with you, that in one morning you suddenly make this change!
translations.idiomatic: and reproaching Murong Chong's sudden ingratitude.

sentences.zh: 」沖命詹事答之，亦稱「皇太弟有令：孤今心在天下，豈顧一袍小惠。

translations.literal: " Chong ordered his household steward to answer, also stating, "The imperial heir younger brother has ordered: We now set Our heart on all under Heaven—how could We care for the small favor of one robe.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong's steward answered that the regent's heart was set on the empire, not on a robe,

sentences.zh: 苟能知命，便可君臣束手，早送皇帝，自當寬貸苻氏，以酬曩好，終不使既往之施獨美於前」。

translations.literal: If you can know fate, then ruler and minister may bind their hands, early send the emperor, and We of course will broadly pardon the Fu clan to repay former good feeling—We will never let the kindness shown in the past alone be beautiful in what went before."
translations.idiomatic: and demanded Fu Jian surrender Murong Wei and accept terms sparing the Fu if they yielded promptly.

sentences.zh: 堅大怒曰：「吾不用王景略、陽平公之言，使白虜敢至於此。」

translations.literal: Jian was greatly angry and said, "We did not use Wang Jinglue and the Duke of Yangping's words, and so the white barbarians dare reach this point."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian raged that ignoring Wang Meng and Fu Rong had let the Murongs get this far.

sentences.zh: 苻丕在鄴糧竭，馬無草，削松木而食之。

translations.literal: Fu Pi at Ye ran out of grain; horses had no fodder; they shaved pine wood and ate it.
translations.idiomatic: Besieged in Ye, Fu Pi fed on shaved pine when grain and fodder ran out.

sentences.zh: 會丁零叛慕容垂，垂引師去鄴，始具西問，知苻睿等喪敗，長安危逼，乃遣其陽平太守邵興率騎一千，將北引重合侯苻謨、高邑侯苻亮、阜城侯苻定於常山，固安侯苻鑒、中山太守王兗于中山，以為己援。

translations.literal: When the Dingling rebelled against Murong Chui, Chui led the army away from Ye, and only then did reliable western news arrive; learning that Fu Rui and the others had been defeated and lost, and that Chang'an was in critical peril, he sent his prefect of Yangping Shao Xing leading one thousand cavalry intending to lead north Marquis of Chonghe Fu Mo, Marquis of Gaoyi Fu Liang, Marquis of Fucheng Fu Ding at Changshan, Marquis of Gu'an Fu Jian the clansman, and prefect of Zhongshan Wang Yan at Zhongshan, to be his supports.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhai Bin's revolt drew Murong Chui off, Fu Pi learned of disasters in Guanzhong and sent Shao Xing to rally kinsmen Fu Mo, Fu Liang, Fu Ding, the Gu'an marquis Fu Jian, and Wang Yan as reinforcements,

sentences.zh: 垂遣將軍張崇要興，獲之于襄國南。

translations.literal: Chui sent general Zhang Chong to intercept Xing and captured him south of Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: but Murong Chui's Zhang Chong ambushed and captured Shao Xing south of Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 又遣其參軍封孚西引張蠔、并州刺史王騰于晉陽，蠔、騰以眾寡不赴。

translations.literal: He also sent his adjutant Feng Fu west to summon Zhang He and inspector of Bingzhou Wang Teng at Jinyang; He and Teng, because their hosts were few, did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi's envoy Feng Fu failed to move Zhang He and Wang Teng from Jinyang for lack of troops.

sentences.zh: 丕進退路窮，乃謀於群僚。

translations.literal: Pi's advance and retreat had no road; he thereupon planned with the host of subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Trapped, Fu Pi consulted his staff.

sentences.zh: 司馬楊膺唱歸順之計，丕猶未從。

translations.literal: Marshal Yang Ying advocated a plan of submission; Pi still did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ying urged surrender to Jin, but Fu Pi hesitated.

sentences.zh: 會晉遣濟北太守丁匡據碻磝，濟陽太守郭滿據滑台，將軍顏肱、劉襲次於河北，丕遣將軍桑據距之，為王師所敗。

translations.literal: When Jin sent prefect of Jibei Ding Kuang to hold Qiao'ao, prefect of Jiyang Guo Man to hold Huatai, generals Yan Gong and Liu Xi halting north of the Yellow River, Pi sent general Sang Ju to oppose them and was defeated by the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Jin seized Qiao'ao and Huatai; Fu Pi's Sang Ju lost to Yan Gong and Liu Xi,

sentences.zh: 襲等進攻黎陽，克之。

translations.literal: Xi and the others advanced and attacked Liyang and took it.
translations.idiomatic: who then stormed Liyang.

sentences.zh: 丕懼，乃遣從弟就與參軍焦逵請救于謝玄。

translations.literal: Pi was afraid and thereupon sent cousin Jiu together with adjutant Jiao Kui to request rescue from Xie Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi then dispatched Fu Jiu and Jiao Kui to beg Xie Xuan for aid.

sentences.zh: 丕書稱假途求糧，還赴國難，須軍援既接，以鄴與之，若西路不通，長安陷沒，請率所領保守鄴城。

translations.literal: Pi's letter claimed borrowing a road to seek grain, returning to answer the state's crisis, and that once military support had joined, he would give Ye; if the western road were blocked and Chang'an fell, he asked to lead what he commanded to hold Ye city secure.
translations.idiomatic: His letter asked passage and grain to relieve Guanzhong, promised Ye once rescued, or holding Ye if Chang'an fell,

sentences.zh: 乃羈縻一方，文降而已。

translations.literal: thereby to tie reins on one corner—a literary surrender only.
translations.idiomatic: framing the plea as a nominal submission.

sentences.zh: 逵與參軍薑讓密謂楊膺曰：「今禍難如此，京師阻隔，吉凶莫審，密邇寇仇，三軍罄絕，傾危之甚，朝不及夕。

translations.literal: Kui secretly together with adjutant Jiang Rang said to Yang Ying, "Now disaster and hardship are thus; the capital is cut off; good or ill cannot be investigated; we press close on bandit foes; the three armies are exhausted; the tilt toward peril is extreme—not even a morning waits for evening.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Kui and Jiang Rang told Yang Ying that Ye was doomed within hours,

sentences.zh: 觀公豪氣不除，非救世之主，既不能竭盡誠款，速致糧援，方設兩端，必無成也。

translations.literal: Observing the duke's bravado not removed, he is not a lord who saves the age; since he cannot exhaust sincere good faith and speedily bring grain support, yet sets up two ends, there will certainly be no success.
translations.idiomatic: that Fu Pi's pride and double game would win no help,

sentences.zh: 今日之殆，疾於轉機，不容虛設，徒成反覆。

translations.literal: Today's peril is swifter than a turning machine; it cannot tolerate empty schemes that only make flip-flop.
translations.idiomatic: and that delay would prove fatal,

sentences.zh: 宜正書為表，以結殷勤。

translations.literal: You ought to straighten the letter into a memorial to knot earnest devotion.
translations.idiomatic: so they should rewrite the plea as a frank memorial of allegiance,

sentences.zh: 若王師之至，必當致身。

translations.literal: If the royal army arrives, you must certainly deliver your person.
translations.idiomatic: promising Fu Pi would yield in person when Jin came,

sentences.zh: 如其不從，可逼縛與之。

translations.literal: If he will not follow, you may bind him by force and hand him over.
translations.idiomatic: or bind Fu Pi and hand him over if he refused,

sentences.zh: 苟不義服，一人力耳。

translations.literal: If he will not righteously submit, it is the strength of one man only.
translations.idiomatic: for one man could overpower him,

sentences.zh: 古人行權，寧濟為功，況君侯累葉載德，顯祖初著名于晉朝，今復建崇勳，使功業相繼，千載一時，不可失也。

translations.literal: Men of old exercised expedients—success was all that mattered; how much more when lord and marquis for accumulated generations have borne virtue, when your illustrious ancestor first made a name in the Jin court, and now again you would raise lofty merit, letting merit continue in succession—once in a thousand ages, it cannot be lost."
translations.idiomatic: and appealed to family ties with Jin to seize the moment.

sentences.zh: 」膺素輕丕，自以力能逼之，乃改書而遣逵等，並遣濟南毛蜀、毛鮮等分房為任于晉。

translations.literal: " Ying had always despised Pi and believed his own strength could coerce him; he thereupon altered the letter and sent Kui and others, and also sent Mao Shu and Mao Xian of Jinan separately to take assignments with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ying, despising Fu Pi, forged a submissive letter and sent hostages to Jin.

sentences.zh: 堅遣鴻臚郝稚征處士王嘉於到獸山。

translations.literal: Jian sent herald Hao Zhi to summon recluse Wang Jia at Mount Daoshou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian sent Hao Zhi to fetch the recluse Wang Jia from Mount Daoshou.

sentences.zh: 既至，堅每日召嘉與道安於外殿，動靜咨問之。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Jian daily summoned Jia together with Dao'an in the outer hall and consulted them on movements and stillness.
translations.idiomatic: He consulted Wang Jia and Dao'an daily in the outer hall.

sentences.zh: 慕容暐入見東堂，稽首謝曰：「弟沖不識義方，孤背國恩，臣罪應萬死。

translations.literal: Murong Wei entered to see him in the east hall, knocked his head in apology, and said, "Younger brother Chong does not know the model of right; alone he has betrayed the state's grace—your subject's crime deserves ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Wei kowtowed, blaming Murong Chong and begging death,

sentences.zh: 陛下垂天地之容，臣蒙更生之惠。

translations.literal: Your Majesty lets fall the countenance of Heaven and earth; your subject receives the favor of renewed life.
translations.idiomatic: thanked Fu Jian for sparing him,

sentences.zh: 臣二子昨婚，明當三日，愚欲暫屈鑾駕，幸臣私第。

translations.literal: Your subject's two sons married yesterday; tomorrow is the third day; foolishly We wish briefly to bend the imperial train to favor your subject's private residence."
translations.idiomatic: and invited Fu Jian to a third-day wedding banquet at his house.

sentences.zh: 」堅許之。

translations.literal: " Jian granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian agreed.

sentences.zh: 暐出，嘉曰：「椎蘆作蘧蒢，不成文章，會天大雨，不得殺羊。

translations.literal: When Wei went out, Jia said, "Pounding reeds to make a quchu mat does not make a pattern; meeting Heaven's great rain, you cannot kill the sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jia chanted an opaque riddle about rush mats and rain,

sentences.zh: 」堅與群臣莫之能解。

translations.literal: Jian together with the host of ministers could not interpret it.
translations.idiomatic: which baffled Fu Jian and the court,

sentences.zh: 是夜大雨，晨不果出。

translations.literal: That night came great rain; at dawn the visit did not take place.
translations.idiomatic: until a night storm scrubbed the planned outing.

sentences.zh: 初，暐之遣諸弟起兵于外也，堅防守甚嚴，謀應之而無因。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wei had sent younger brothers to raise troops outside, Jian's defense was very strict; they plotted to respond but had no opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Wei had long schemed against tight Qin security,

sentences.zh: 時鮮卑在城者猶有千餘人，暐乃密結鮮卑之眾，謀伏兵請堅，因而殺之。

translations.literal: At that time there were still more than a thousand Xianbei in the city; Wei thereupon secretly bound the Xianbei host, plotted ambush soldiers, invited Jian, and thereby would kill him.
translations.idiomatic: and now secretly rallied a thousand Xianbei to ambush Fu Jian at the banquet,

sentences.zh: 令其豪帥悉羅騰、屈突鐵侯等潛告之曰：「官今使侯外鎮，聽舊人悉隨，可於某日會集某處。

translations.literal: He ordered their chieftains Xiluo Teng, Qutu Tiehou, and others secretly to tell them, "The officials now order you to garrison outside; they listen to all old followers to follow—on a certain day assemble at a certain place."
translations.idiomatic: telling Xianbei leaders they were being sent out of the city on a set day to gather,

sentences.zh: 」鮮卑信之。

translations.literal: " The Xianbei believed it.
translations.idiomatic: and the Xianbei believed the lie.

sentences.zh: 北部人突賢與其妹別，妹為左將軍竇沖小妻，聞以告沖，請留其兄。

translations.literal: A northerner named Tuxian took leave of his younger sister; his younger sister was the junior wife of left general Dou Chong; hearing it she told Chong and asked to keep her elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Tuxian's sister, a concubine of Dou Chong, leaked the plot,

sentences.zh: 沖馳入白堅，堅大驚，召騰問之，騰具首服。

translations.literal: Chong galloped in to report to Jian; Jian was greatly startled, summoned Teng and questioned him; Teng fully confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chong raced to Fu Jian; Xiluo Teng confessed under interrogation,

sentences.zh: 堅乃誅暐父子及其宗族，城內鮮卑無少長及婦女皆殺之。

translations.literal: Jian thereupon executed Wei, father and son, and their whole clan; within the city Xianbei, young and old without distinction, together with women, were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: and Fu Jian slaughtered every Murong and every Xianbei in Chang'an, women and children included.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂復圍鄴城。

translations.literal: Murong Chui again besieged Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui renewed the siege of Ye.

sentences.zh: 焦逵既至，朝廷果欲征丕任子，然後出師。

translations.literal: When Jiao Kui arrived, the court indeed wished to demand Fu Pi's hostage son and only then send troops.
translations.idiomatic: At court some wanted a hostage from Fu Pi before aiding him,

sentences.zh: 逵固陳丕款誠無貳，並宣楊膺之意，乃遣劉牢之等率眾二萬，水陸運漕救鄴。

translations.literal: Kui firmly stated Pi's sincere good faith was without duplicity, and also declared Yang Ying's intent; thereupon they sent Liu Laizhi and others leading twenty thousand, transporting grain by water and land to rescue Ye.
translations.idiomatic: but Jiao Kui vouched for Fu Pi's sincerity and Yang Ying's offer, so Jin sent Liu Laizhi with twenty thousand men and grain to relieve Ye.

sentences.zh: 時長安大饑，人相食，諸將歸而吐肉以飴妻子。

translations.literal: At that time Chang'an had great famine; men ate one another; generals returning vomited meat to feed wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Chang'an starved until people cannibalized one another and soldiers regurgitated meat for their families,

sentences.zh: 慕容沖僭稱尊號于阿房，改年更始。

translations.literal: Murong Chong usurped the supreme title at Epang and changed the era to Gengshi.
translations.idiomatic: while Murong Chong declared himself emperor at Epang under a new era name.

sentences.zh: 堅與沖戰，各有勝負。

translations.literal: Jian fought with Chong; each side had victory and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian and Murong Chong traded wins and losses,

sentences.zh: 嘗為沖軍所圍，殿中上將軍鄧邁、左中郎將鄧綏、尚書郎鄧瓊相謂曰：「吾門世荷榮寵，先君建殊功於國家，不可不立忠效節，以成先君之志。

translations.literal: Once he was surrounded by Chong's army; palace senior general Deng Mai, left middle general Deng Sui, and secretary gentleman Deng Qiong said to one another, "Our gate for generations has borne glory and favor; the former lord built extraordinary merit for the state—we cannot fail to establish loyalty and show integrity, thereby completing the former lord's purpose.
translations.idiomatic: until Murong Chong trapped Fu Jian; the Deng cousins resolved to die for the throne their fathers had served,

sentences.zh: 且不死君難者，非丈夫也。

translations.literal: Moreover one who does not die in the ruler's crisis is not a real man.
translations.idiomatic: declaring that gentlemen die with their sovereign,

sentences.zh: 」於是與毛長樂等蒙獸皮，奮矛而擊沖軍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon together with Mao Changle and others they draped beast skins, grasped spears, and struck Chong's army.
translations.idiomatic: donned hides and charged Murong Chong's line,

sentences.zh: 沖軍潰，堅獲免，嘉其忠勇，並拜五校，加三品將軍，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Chong's army broke; Jian was spared capture; he praised their loyalty and courage, concurrently appointed them all five-colonel posts, added third-rank general, bestowed noble rank marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Their sortie broke Murong Chong's ring and earned them rapid promotion,

sentences.zh: 沖又遣其尚書令高蓋率眾夜襲長安，攻陷南門，入於南城。

translations.literal: Chong again sent his director of the secretariat Gao Gai leading a host by night to raid Chang'an, stormed the south gate, and entered the south city.
translations.idiomatic: but Murong Chong sent Gao Gai in a night attack that breached the south gate,

sentences.zh: 左將軍竇沖、前禁將軍李辯等擊敗之，斬首千八百級，分其屍而食之。

translations.literal: Left general Dou Chong, forward prohibition general Li Bian, and others defeated them, beheaded one thousand eight hundred grades, and divided their corpses and ate them.
translations.idiomatic: until Dou Chong and Li Bian slaughtered eighteen hundred attackers and devoured the dead,

sentences.zh: 堅尋敗沖於城西，追奔至於阿城。

translations.literal: Jian soon defeated Chong west of the city, pursued the rout as far as Acheng.
translations.idiomatic: then Fu Jian drove Murong Chong back to Acheng.

sentences.zh: 諸將請乘勝入城，堅懼為沖所獲，乃擊金以止軍。

translations.literal: The generals requested to exploit victory and enter the city; Jian feared being captured by Chong and thereupon struck metal to halt the army.
translations.idiomatic: Generals wanted to storm Epang, but Fu Jian, fearing ambush, sounded the recall,

sentences.zh: 是時劉牢之至枋頭。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Laizhi reached Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Liu Laizhi's relief column reached Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 征東參軍徐義、宦人孟豐告苻丕，楊膺、薑讓等謀反，丕收膺、讓戮之。

translations.literal: Eastern expedition adjutant Xu Yi and eunuch Meng Feng reported to Fu Pi that Yang Ying, Jiang Rang, and others plotted rebellion; Pi seized Ying and Rang and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: In Ye, eastern-expedition adjutant Xu Yi and the eunuch Meng Feng accused Yang Ying and Jiang Rang of plotting treason, whereupon Fu Pi arrested and executed both men.

sentences.zh: 牢之以丕自相屠戮，盤桓不進。

translations.literal: Laizhi, because Pi was slaughtering one another within, hesitated and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laizhi held his column back once Fu Pi began executing his own advisers.

sentences.zh: 苻暉屢為沖所敗，堅讓之曰：「汝，吾之子也，擁大眾，屢為白虜小兒所摧，何用生為！

translations.literal: Fu Hui was repeatedly defeated by Chong; Jian rebuked him, saying, "You are Our son, yet embrace a great host and are repeatedly shattered by the white-barbarian boys—what use is living!"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hui kept losing to Murong Chong, so Fu Jian reviled him as a useless son who could not beat the Murong “children.”

sentences.zh: 」暉憤恚自殺。

translations.literal: Hui, angry and bitter, killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated, Fu Hui took his own life.

sentences.zh: 關中堡壁三千餘所，推平遠將軍馮翊、趙敖為統主，相率結盟，遣兵糧助堅。

translations.literal: More than three thousand fort stockades in Guanzhong pushed Fengyi’s general who pacifies the distance Zhao Ao as chief commander, jointly swore alliance, and sent troops and grain to aid Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Over three thousand Guanzhong forts rallied behind Zhao Ao of Fanyi, swore mutual aid, and convoyed supplies to Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 左將軍苟池、右將軍俱石子率騎五千，與沖爭麥，戰於驪山，為沖所敗，池死之，石子奔鄴。

translations.literal: Left general Gou Chi and right general Ju Shizi led five thousand cavalry to contend for wheat with Chong, fought at Mount Li, were defeated by Chong—Chi died in it, Shizi fled to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Chi and Ju Shizi took five thousand horse to seize the wheat fields on Lishan, lost to Murong Chong, and left Gou Chi dead and Ju Shizi running for Ye.

sentences.zh: 堅大怒，復遣領軍楊定率左右精騎二千五百擊沖，大敗之，俘掠鮮卑萬餘而還。

translations.literal: Jian was greatly angry again and sent guard general Yang Ding leading twenty-five hundred picked cavalry of the left and right to strike Chong, greatly defeated him, captured and plundered more than ten thousand Xianbei and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian then sent Yang Ding with twenty-five hundred elite riders who routed Murong Chong and brought back ten thousand Xianbei captives.

sentences.zh: 堅怒，悉坑之。

translations.literal: Jian was angry and had them all buried in pits.
translations.idiomatic: In a fury Fu Jian had those prisoners massacred in burial pits.

sentences.zh: 定果勇善戰，沖深憚之，遂穿馬埳以自固。

translations.literal: Ding was truly brave and skilled in battle; Chong deeply feared him, thereupon dug horse moats to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ding’s prowess terrified Murong Chong into digging cavalry traps around his camp.

sentences.zh: 劉牢之至鄴，慕容垂北如新城。

translations.literal: When Liu Laizhi reached Ye, Murong Chui went north toward Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laizhi’s arrival at Ye drew Murong Chui north toward Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 鄴中饑甚，丕率鄴城之眾就晉谷於枋頭。

translations.literal: Ye was extremely hungry; Pi led Ye city’s host to take Jin grain at Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: Starving Ye surrendered its garrison to Jin grain ships at Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 牢之入屯鄴城。

translations.literal: Laizhi entered and garrisoned Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laizhi marched in and occupied Ye.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂軍人饑甚，多奔中山，幽、冀人相食。

translations.literal: Murong Chui’s soldiers were extremely hungry; many fled to Zhongshan; You and Ji people ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui’s army starved until men bolted for Zhongshan and cannibalism spread through You and Ji.

sentences.zh: 初，關東謠曰：「幽州𡙇，生當滅。

translations.literal: Earlier a ditty east of the pass said, "Youzhou 𡙇—born, it must perish.
translations.idiomatic: A Hebei rhyme had long warned that “Youzhou 𡙇” must die—

sentences.zh: 若不滅，百姓絕。

translations.literal: If it does not perish, the black-haired people will be cut off."
translations.idiomatic: and that otherwise the people would be wiped out altogether.”

sentences.zh: 」𡙇，垂之本名。

translations.literal: 𡙇 is Chui’s original given name.
translations.idiomatic: The graph stood for Murong Chui’s birth name.

sentences.zh: 與丕相持經年，百姓死幾絕。

translations.literal: He and Pi faced each other for a full year; the common people died until nearly extinct.
translations.idiomatic: A year’s stalemate between Murong Chui and Fu Pi left the countryside almost depopulated.

sentences.zh: 先是，姚萇攻新平，新平太守苟輔將降之，郡人遼西太守馮傑、蓮勺令馮翊等諫曰：「天下喪亂，忠臣乃見。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yao Chang attacked Xinping, Xinping prefect Gou Fu was about to surrender; men of the commandery—Liaoxi prefect Feng Jie, Lianzhuo magistrate Feng Yi, and others—remonstrated, saying, "All under Heaven is in ruin and chaos—only then do loyal ministers appear.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chang besieged Xinping, Prefect Gou Fu wavered on surrender until Feng Jie and Feng Yi reminded him that loyal ministers shine in chaos,

sentences.zh: 昔田單守一城而存齊，今秦之所有，猶連州累鎮，郡國百城。

translations.literal: In the past Tian Dan defended one city and preserved Qi; now what Qin still holds links province after province and fort after fort—hundred cities of commanderies and states.
translations.idiomatic: citing Tian Dan’s single-city defense of Qi and noting that Qin still held a hundred linked cities,

sentences.zh: 臣子之于君父，盡心焉，盡力焉，死而後已，豈宜貳哉！

translations.literal: Between subject and son and ruler and father one exhausts heart, exhausts strength, and only then stops—how can one be of two minds!"
translations.idiomatic: and that a servant owes his prince every ounce of loyalty unto death.

sentences.zh: 」輔大悅，於是憑城固守。

translations.literal: Fu was greatly pleased and thereupon relied on the city and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Heartened, Gou Fu chose to hold the walls.

sentences.zh: 萇為土山地道，輔亦為之。

translations.literal: Chang made earthen hills and tunnel ways; Fu also made them.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang piled siege ramps and sapped tunnels; Gou Fu countered with the same.

sentences.zh: 或戰山峰，萇眾死者萬有餘人。

translations.literal: Sometimes they fought on the heights; more than ten thousand of Chang’s host died.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting on the ridges cost Yao Chang over ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 輔乃詐降，萇將入，覺之，引眾而退。

translations.literal: Fu thereupon feigned surrender; when Chang was about to enter, he detected it and led the host and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Fu’s sham capitulation nearly lured Yao Chang inside before he sensed the trap and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 輔馳出擊之，斬獲萬計。

translations.literal: Fu galloped out and struck them, beheading and capturing on the order of ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Fu sallied and killed or captured nearly ten thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 至是，糧竭矢盡，外救不至，萇遣吏謂輔曰：「吾方以義取天下，豈仇忠臣乎？

translations.literal: By this time grain was exhausted and arrows were gone, outside rescue did not arrive; Chang sent an official to tell Fu, "We are about to take all under Heaven by righteousness—how could We hate loyal ministers?
translations.idiomatic: When supplies and arrows failed and no relief came, Yao Chang’s envoy swore he bore no grudge against loyalty,

sentences.zh: 卿但率見眾男女還長婁，吾須此城置鎮。

translations.literal: You need only lead the men and women of your visible host back to Changlou; We need this city to set a garrison."
translations.idiomatic: and asked Gou Fu to march every civilian out to “Changlou” so he could garrison the town—

sentences.zh: 」輔以為然，率男女萬五千口出城，萇圍而坑之，男女無遺。

translations.literal: Fu thought it right, led fifteen thousand men and women out of the city, and Chang surrounded them and buried them in pits—men and women none survived.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting Yao Chang’s pledge, Gou Fu marched fifteen thousand civilians out of the walls; Yao Chang ringed them and buried every soul alive.

sentences.zh: 初，石季龍末，清河崔悅為新平相，為郡人所殺。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the end of Shi Jilong, Qinghe’s Cui Yue was prefect of Xinping and was killed by men of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Years before, Prefect Cui Yue of Qinghe had been murdered by Xinping locals under Later Zhao,

sentences.zh: 悅子液後仕堅，為尚書郎，自表父仇不同天地，請還冀州。

translations.literal: Yue’s son Ye later served Jian as secretary gentleman and personally memorialized that his father’s enemy was not shared under Heaven with him, requesting return to Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: and his son Cui Ye later served Fu Jian until he begged leave to avenge his father’s blood feud.

sentences.zh: 堅湣之，禁錮新平人，缺其城角以恥之。

translations.literal: Jian pitied him, shackled Xinping people, and broke a corner of their city wall to shame them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian pitied Cui Ye, humiliated Xinping by cropping its wall, and kept its notables under stigma,

sentences.zh: 新平酋望深以為慚，故相率距萇，以立忠義。

translations.literal: Xinping’s chiefs and notables deeply took it as shame; therefore they jointly resisted Chang to establish loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: which spurred Xinping’s gentry to resist Yao Chang to the death.

sentences.zh: 時有群烏數萬，翔鳴于長安城上，其聲甚悲，占者以為鬥羽不終年，有甲兵入城之象。

translations.literal: At that time flocks of crows in the tens of thousands circled crying atop Chang’an’s walls; their sound was very mournful—diviners took it as fighting feathers not lasting a year, an image of armored troops entering the city.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand crows wheeling above Chang’an shrieking like battle omens foretold steel inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 沖率眾登城，堅身貫甲胄，督戰距之，飛矢滿身，血流被體。

translations.literal: Chong led the host scaling the wall; Jian personally donned armor, supervised battle to oppose them—flying arrows covered his body, blood flow soaked his frame.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong stormed the battlements while Fu Jian, armored and arrow-riddled, led the defense in person.

sentences.zh: 時雖兵寇危逼，馮翊諸堡壁猶有負糧冒難而至者，多為賊所殺。

translations.literal: Though at the time armed bandits pressed critically, the Fengyi stockades still had men who bore grain braving hardship to come—most were killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Even under siege, loyal forts in Fanyi tried to smuggle grain to Chang’an, though Murong’s pickets killed most couriers.

sentences.zh: 堅謂之曰：「聞來者率不善達，誠是忠臣赴難之義。

translations.literal: Jian said to them, "We hear those who come mostly do not arrive safely—truly it is the righteousness of loyal ministers rushing to crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian told survivors that their loyalty shone though few got through,

sentences.zh: 當今寇難殷繁，非一人之力所能濟也。

translations.literal: Now bandit hardship is thick and manifold; it is not strength one man can remedy.
translations.idiomatic: and that the crisis was beyond any single man’s strength,

sentences.zh: 庶明靈有照，禍極災返，善保誠順，為國自愛，蓄糧厲甲，端聽師期，不可徒喪無成，相隨獸口。

translations.literal: Perhaps the bright spirits have regard—when woe reaches the limit, disaster turns back; take good care, keep true and compliant, for the state cherish yourselves, store grain, harden armor, uprightly await the army’s date—do not vainly perish without success and together fall into beasts’ mouths."
translations.idiomatic: begging them to husband strength, hoard grain and armor, and wait for a concerted rising instead of throwing themselves away.

sentences.zh: 」三輔人為沖所略者，咸遣使告堅，請放火以為內應。

translations.literal: Those of the three approaches whom Chong had plundered all sent messengers telling Jian, asking to set fires to be inner response.
translations.idiomatic: People Murong Chong had dragged from the Guanzhong heartland offered to light fires inside his camps as signals for Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「哀諸卿忠誠之意也，何復已已。

translations.literal: Jian said, "We pity you gentlemen’s intent of loyalty—why go further.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian thanked them but refused,

sentences.zh: 但時運圮喪，恐無益于國，空使諸卿坐自夷滅，吾所不忍也。

translations.literal: But the times’ fortune is ruined; We fear it will not benefit the state and will only make you gentlemen sit and be extinguished to no purpose—what We cannot bear."
translations.idiomatic: fearing their arson would only annihilate loyalists without helping the throne.

sentences.zh: 且吾精兵若獸，利器如霜，而衄于烏合疲鈍之賊，豈非天也！

translations.literal: Moreover Our crack troops are like beasts, sharp weapons like frost—yet we stumble against a tired, dull mob in a flock; is it not Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: He added that crack Qin troops should not lose to rabble unless Heaven willed it,

sentences.zh: 宜善思之。

translations.literal: You ought to think well on it."
translations.idiomatic: and asked them to reconsider.

sentences.zh: 」眾固請曰：「臣等不愛性命，投身為國，若上天有靈，單誠或冀一濟，沒無遺恨矣。

translations.literal: The host firmly requested, saying, "Your subjects do not spare their lives, casting bodies for the state; if High Heaven has spirit, perhaps single-minded sincerity may hope for one relief—dying leaves no regret."
translations.idiomatic: They insisted they would gladly die for a chance at success,

sentences.zh: 」堅遣騎七百應之。

translations.literal: Jian sent seven hundred cavalry to respond to them.
translations.idiomatic: so Fu Jian sent seven hundred riders to coordinate.

sentences.zh: 而沖營放火者為風焰所燒，其能免者十有一二。

translations.literal: Yet those who set fire in Chong’s camp were burned by wind and flame; of those who could escape, only one or two in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Wind whipped Murong Chong’s own fires back on the volunteers, killing nine in ten.

sentences.zh: 堅深痛之，身為設祭而招之曰：「有忠有靈，來就此庭。

translations.literal: Jian deeply grieved for them, personally set offerings for them and summoned, saying, "Loyal and numinous, come to this court.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian held a public requiem, calling the spirits of the dead to his courtyard,

sentences.zh: 歸汝先父，勿為妖形。

translations.literal: Return to your former fathers; do not take monstrous forms."
translations.idiomatic: asking them to rest with their ancestors and cease haunting as demons,

sentences.zh: 」歔欷流涕，悲不自勝。

translations.literal: He sobbed and wept, grief he could not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: and wept until he could not contain himself.

sentences.zh: 眾咸相謂曰：「至尊慈恩如此，吾等有死無移。

translations.literal: The host all said to one another, "The supreme one’s kindly grace is thus—with death we shall not shift."
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers vowed they would die for such a sovereign,

sentences.zh: 」沖毒暴關中，人皆流散，道路斷絕，千里無煙。

translations.literal: Chong was venomous and cruel in Guanzhong; people all scattered; roads were cut off; for a thousand li no smoke.
translations.idiomatic: while Murong Chong’s cruelty emptied the roads for a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 堅以甘松護軍仇騰為馮翊太守，加輔國將軍，與破虜將軍蜀人蘭犢慰勉馮翊諸縣之眾。

translations.literal: Jian made Gansong guard general Qiu Teng prefect of Fanyi, added general who aids the state, together with general who breaks captives Lan Du of Shu to comfort and encourage the hosts of Fengyi’s counties.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Qiu Teng and the Shu general Lan Du to rally Fanyi’s counties.

sentences.zh: 眾咸曰：「與陛下同死共生，誓無有貳。」

translations.literal: The host all said, "With Your Majesty we die and live together—we swear there is no second mind."
translations.idiomatic: The militias swore to live or die with him alone.

sentences.zh: 每夜有周城大呼曰：「楊定健兒應屬我，宮殿台觀應坐我，父子同出不共汝。

translations.literal: Each night someone shouted circling the wall, "Yang Ding’s brave lads belong to me; palace halls and terraces I should sit in; father and son go out together—I will not share with you."
translations.idiomatic: Nightly voices circled Chang’an claiming Yang Ding’s veterans and the palace for themselves,

sentences.zh: 」且尋而不見人跡。

translations.literal: Yet when searched for, no human tracks were found.
translations.idiomatic: yet searches found no one.

sentences.zh: 城中有書曰《古符傳賈錄》，載「帝出五將久長得」。

translations.literal: In the city was a book called Ancient Talisman Record of Jia, recording "The emperor goes out to the Five Generals and long survives."
translations.idiomatic: A prophetic book in the city read “The Son of Heaven flees to the Five Generals Mountain and endures long.”

sentences.zh: 先是，又謠曰：「堅入五將山長得。

translations.literal: Earlier there was also a ditty, "Jian enters Five Generals Mountain and long survives."
translations.idiomatic: A street rhyme had said Fu Jian would find life on Five Generals Mountain,

sentences.zh: 」堅大信之，告其太子宏曰：「脫如此言，天或導予。

translations.literal: Jian greatly believed it, told his heir apparent Hong, "If this saying comes true, Heaven perhaps guides Us.
translations.idiomatic: so Fu Jian told Crown Prince Fu Hong he meant to obey Heaven’s roadmap,

sentences.zh: 今留汝兼總戎政，勿與賊爭利，朕當出隴收兵運糧以給汝。

translations.literal: Now We leave you to oversee all military affairs jointly; do not contend profit with the bandits; We shall go out Long to collect troops and transport grain to supply you.
translations.idiomatic: charging Hong to avoid risky sorties while he himself rode to Long to raise reinforcements and grain,

sentences.zh: 天其或者正訓予也。

translations.literal: Heaven perhaps is just instructing Us."
translations.idiomatic: calling the retreat Heaven’s lesson.

sentences.zh: 」於是遣衛將軍楊定擊沖於城西，為沖所擒。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent guard general Yang Ding to strike Chong west of the city; he was captured by Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He first sent Yang Ding west of the city, but Murong Chong captured him.

sentences.zh: 堅彌懼，付宏以後事，將中山公詵、張夫人率騎數百出如五將，宣告州郡，期以孟冬救長安。

translations.literal: Jian was all the more afraid, handed Hong the later affairs, and with Duke of Zhongshan Shen and Lady Zhang led several hundred cavalry out toward Five Generals, proclaiming to provinces and commanderies, fixing first month of winter to relieve Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: Terror-stricken, he entrusted the capital to Fu Hong and rode toward Five Generals Mountain with Fu Shen, Lady Zhang, and a few hundred horse, promising a winter relief campaign.

sentences.zh: 宏尋將母妻宗室男女數千騎出奔，百僚逃散。

translations.literal: Hong soon led mother, wives, and several thousand riders of the imperial clan out in flight; the hundred officials scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hong promptly fled with the women of the harem and thousands of clansmen while the bureaucracy evaporated.

sentences.zh: 慕容沖入據長安，從兵大掠，死者不可勝計。

translations.literal: Murong Chong entered and held Chang’an; following troops plundered greatly; the dead could not be reckoned.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong’s horde sacked Chang’an beyond counting of corpses.

sentences.zh: 初，秦之未亂也，關中土然，無火而煙氣大起，方數十里中，月餘不滅。

translations.literal: Earlier, before Qin’s disorders, within Guanzhong the earth smoldered—without fire yet great smoke arose, covering several tens of li square, for more than a month without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Before the war smoke had risen from bare earth across dozens of li for a month—an uncanny omen.

sentences.zh: 堅每臨聽訟觀，令百姓有怨者舉煙於城北，觀而錄之。

translations.literal: Whenever Jian came to the hall for hearing lawsuits, he ordered that commoners with grievances raise smoke north of the city; he observed and recorded them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian had once invited citizens to signal injustice with smoke north of town,

sentences.zh: 長安為之語曰：「欲得必存當舉煙。

translations.literal: Chang’an made a saying of it: "If you wish to survive, you must raise smoke."
translations.idiomatic: so Chang’an joked that survival meant lighting warning fires,

sentences.zh: 」又為謠曰：「長鞘馬鞭擊左股，太歲南行當復虜。

translations.literal: There was also a ditty: "Long-scabbard horsewhip strikes the left thigh; Grand Year southward march shall again capture the white barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: while another rhyme spoke of whips, the planet Tai Sui, and capturing “white barbarians”—

sentences.zh: 」秦人呼鮮卑為白虜。

translations.literal: Qin people called the Xianbei white barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Qin slang for Murong’s Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂之起於關東，歲在癸末。

translations.literal: When Murong Chui rose east of the pass, the year was in guiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui’s rebellion came in the guiwei year,

sentences.zh: 堅之分氐戶于諸鎮也，趙整因侍，援琴而歌曰：「阿得脂，阿得脂，博勞舊父是仇綏，尾長翼短不能飛，遠徙種人留鮮卑，一旦緩急語阿誰！

translations.literal: When Jian divided Di households to the various garrisons, Zhao Zheng, taking advantage of attendance, grasped the zither and sang, "A-de-zhi, a-de-zhi—the shrike’s old father is Chou Sui; tail long, wings short, cannot fly; far-moved kindred stay while Xianbei remain—once urgent and slack, whom will you tell!"
translations.idiomatic: and when Fu Jian scattered Di colonists Zhao Zheng had sung a nonsense song mocking Di tails and Xianbei wings,

sentences.zh: 」堅笑而不納。

translations.literal: Jian laughed and did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: which Fu Jian laughed off,

sentences.zh: 至是，整言驗矣。

translations.literal: By this time Zheng’s words were verified.
translations.idiomatic: until every line came true.

sentences.zh: 堅至五將山，姚萇遣將軍吳忠圍之。

translations.literal: When Jian reached Five Generals Mountain, Yao Chang sent general Wu Zhong to surround him.
translations.idiomatic: At Five Generals Mountain Yao Chang’s general Wu Zhong ringed Fu Jian’s camp.

sentences.zh: 堅眾奔散，獨侍御十數人而已。

translations.literal: Jian’s host fled and scattered; only a dozen or so attendants remained.
translations.idiomatic: The last retainers melted away until a handful of chamber attendants stayed.

sentences.zh: 神色自若，坐而待之，召宰人進食。

translations.literal: His spirit and bearing were as if normal; he sat and awaited them, summoning the cook to bring food.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian kept his composure, sat waiting, and called for a meal,

sentences.zh: 俄而忠至，執堅以歸新平，幽之於別室。

translations.literal: Shortly Wu Zhong arrived, seized Jian, and returned him to Xinping, imprisoning him in a separate room.
translations.idiomatic: until Wu Zhong seized him and locked him in Xinping,

sentences.zh: 萇求傳國璽於堅曰：「萇次膺符曆，可以為惠。

translations.literal: Chang sought the transmission seal from Jian, saying, "Chang is next to receive the talisman sequence—can you grant it as a favor."
translations.idiomatic: where Yao Chang demanded the jade seal, claiming the mandate now fell to him,

sentences.zh: 」堅瞋目叱之曰：「小羌乃敢幹逼天子，豈以傳國璽授汝羌也，圖緯符命，何所依據？

translations.literal: Jian glared and shouted at him, saying, "Little Qiang dare coerce the Son of Heaven—could We give the transmission seal to you Qiang! Charts and registers, on what do they rely?
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian glared and called him a petty Qiang usurper with no claim to the heirloom,

sentences.zh: 五胡次序，無汝羌名。

translations.literal: In the Five Hu order there is no Qiang name.
translations.idiomatic: citing the old “Five Hu” roll that never listed the Qiang,

sentences.zh: 違天不祥，其能久乎！

translations.literal: To oppose Heaven is inauspicious—can you last long!
translations.idiomatic: and swore Heaven would punish such treason,

sentences.zh: 璽已送晉，不可得也。

translations.literal: The seal has already been sent to Jin—it cannot be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: insisting the true seal was already bound for Jin.

sentences.zh: 」萇又遣尹緯說堅，求為堯、舜禪代之事。

translations.literal: Chang again sent Yin Wei to persuade Jian, seeking the matter of Yao and Shun’s abdication in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang then sent Yin Wei urging a Yao-Shun style abdication,

sentences.zh: 堅責緯曰：「禪代者，聖賢之事。

translations.literal: Jian rebuked Wei, saying, "Abdication in succession is the affair of sages and worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian retorted that abdication belonged to sages,

sentences.zh: 姚萇叛賊，奈何擬之古人！

translations.literal: Yao Chang is a rebel bandit—how dare you compare him to the ancients!"
translations.idiomatic: not to a traitor like Yao Chang,

sentences.zh: 」堅既不許萇以禪代，罵而求死，萇乃縊堅于新平佛寺中，時年四十八。

translations.literal: Since Jian would not grant Chang abdication-in-succession but cursed and sought death, Chang thereupon strangled Jian in a Xinping Buddhist monastery—his years forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: and when Fu Jian kept defying and demanding death, Yao Chang strangled him in a Xinping monastery at age forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 中山公詵及張夫人並自殺。

translations.literal: Duke of Zhongshan Shen and Lady Zhang both killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shen and Lady Zhang killed themselves with him.

sentences.zh: 是歲太元十年也。

translations.literal: That year was the tenth year of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: It was the tenth year of the Jin Taiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 宏之奔也，歸其南秦州刺史楊璧于下辯，璧距之，乃奔武翥氐豪強熙，假道歸順，朝廷處宏于江州。

translations.literal: When Hong fled, he went to his southern Qinzhou inspector Yang Bi at Xiabian; Bi refused him, so he fled to Wuzhu Di chieftain Qiang Xi, borrowed a road to submit, and the court settled Hong at Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hong first sought Yang Bi at Xiabian, was turned away, detoured through Wudu Di territory to surrender to Jin, and was parked at Jiangzhou,

sentences.zh: 宏歷位元輔國將軍。

translations.literal: Hong rose through offices to general who aids the state.
translations.idiomatic: where he rose to general who aids the state,

sentences.zh: 桓玄篡位，以宏為梁州刺史。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan usurped the throne, he made Hong inspector of Liang province.
translations.idiomatic: later named Liangzhou inspector under Huan Xuan’s usurpation,

sentences.zh: 義熙初，以謀叛被誅。

translations.literal: At the start of Yixi he was executed for plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: and executed early in the Yixi era for plotting revolt.

sentences.zh: 初，堅強盛之時，國有童謠云：「河水清復清，苻詔死新城。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jian was at his strongest, a children’s ditty in the state said, "The river water clears again and clears—Fu Zhao dies at Xincheng."
translations.idiomatic: Children’s songs from Fu Jian’s zenith had foretold a “Fu Zhao” dying at Xincheng,

sentences.zh: 」堅聞而惡之，每征伐，戒軍候云：「地有名新者避之。

translations.literal: Jian heard it and detested it; whenever he campaigned, he warned army scouts, "Where the land has a place name with ‘new,’ avoid it."
translations.idiomatic: so he ordered armies to skirt every place called “New,”

sentences.zh: 」時又童謠云：「阿堅連牽三十年，若後欲敗當在江、淮間。

translations.literal: At that time there was also a children’s ditty, "A-Jian dragged along thirty years; if later he wishes defeat, it will be between the Yangtze and Huai."
translations.idiomatic: while another rhyme tied his twenty-seven-year reign to disaster on the Huai line,

sentences.zh: 」堅在位二十七年，因壽春之敗，其國大亂，後二年，竟死于新平佛寺，咸應謠言矣。

translations.literal: Jian held the throne twenty-seven years; because of the defeat at Shouchun his state fell into great chaos; after two more years he indeed died in a Xinping Buddhist monastery—all matched the ditties.
translations.idiomatic: which proved true: twenty-seven years of rule, the Feishui debacle, and death two years later in Xinping matched every omen.

sentences.zh: 丕僭號，偽追諡堅曰世祖宣昭皇帝。

translations.literal: When Pi usurped title, he falsely posthumously honored Jian as Emperor Shizhao of the Shizu line.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Pi declared himself emperor he canonized Fu Jian posthumously as Shizu’s “Shining Manifest” emperor.

sentences.zh: 王猛

translations.literal: Wang Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng.

sentences.zh: 王猛，字景略，北海劇人也，家于魏郡。

translations.literal: Wang Meng, style Jinglue, was a man of Ju in Beihai, his family dwelling in Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng, courtesy name Jinglue, came from Ju county in Beihai but had settled his household in Wei commandery,

sentences.zh: 少貧賤，以鬻畚為業。

translations.literal: In youth he was poor and lowly, and took selling hampers as his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: growing up in poverty he earned a living peddling carrying baskets,

sentences.zh: 嘗貨畚於洛陽，乃有一人貴買其畚，而雲無直，自言：「家去此無遠，可隨我取直。

translations.literal: Once he sold hampers at Luoyang; then there was one man who expensively bought his hampers yet said he had no cash, himself saying, "My home is not far from here—you may follow me to get cash."
translations.idiomatic: and once in Luoyang a customer overpaid for his baskets yet claimed to have no money on hand, inviting him home to collect payment.

sentences.zh: 」猛利其貴而從之，行不覺遠，忽至深山，見一父老，鬚髮皓然，踞胡床而坐，左右十許人，有一人引猛進拜之。

translations.literal: Meng prized the high price and followed him; walking, he did not notice distance; suddenly he reached a deep mountain, saw an old man, beard and hair hoary white, sitting astride a folding stool, about ten men to left and right; one man led Meng forward to bow to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng took the bait of an inflated price and followed the buyer into the hills until they came to a white-haired patriarch enthroned on a camp stool with a handful of attendants.

sentences.zh: 父老曰：「王公何緣拜也！

translations.literal: The old man said, "What reason has Lord Wang to bow!"
translations.idiomatic: The elder waved off his prostration, asking why a future lord should bow,

sentences.zh: 」乃十倍償畚直，遣人送之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he repaid tenfold the hamper price and sent men to escort him back.
translations.idiomatic: then paid ten times the asking price and sent him home with an escort.

sentences.zh: 猛既出，顧視，乃嵩高山也。

translations.literal: When Meng had gone out, he looked back—it was Mount Song of the heights.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back, Wang Meng realized he had been on Mount Song,

sentences.zh: 猛瑰姿俊偉。

translations.literal: Meng had a striking form, handsome and grand.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng was strikingly tall and handsome,

sentences.zh: 博學好兵書，謹重嚴毅，氣度雄遠，細事不幹其慮，自不參其神契，略不與交通，是以浮華之士咸輕而笑之。

translations.literal: Broadly learned, he loved military writings, was prudent, weighty, stern, and firm; his bearing was heroic and far-reaching; petty matters did not trouble his thoughts; unless persons matched his spiritual affinity, he absolutely did not associate with them—therefore flashy gentlemen all belittled and laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: well read in the military classics, grave and aloof, disdainful of petty company, which made fashionable men mock him,

sentences.zh: 猛悠然自得，不以屑懷。

translations.literal: Meng was leisurely content and did not take it to heart in crumbs.
translations.idiomatic: yet he remained serenely indifferent to their scorn.

sentences.zh: 少游于鄴都，時人罕能識也。

translations.literal: In youth he roamed Ye capital; men of the time rarely could recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he wandered Ye, little noticed by contemporaries,

sentences.zh: 惟徐統見而奇之，召為功曹。

translations.literal: Only Xu Tong saw him and thought him extraordinary, summoned him as merit clerk.
translations.idiomatic: until Xu Tong singled him out and offered him a clerkship,

sentences.zh: 遁而不應，遂隱于華陰山。

translations.literal: He slipped away and did not respond, thereupon hid on Mount Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: which he declined, preferring reclusion on Mount Huayin,

sentences.zh: 懷佐世之志，希龍顏之主，斂翼待時，候風雲而後動。

translations.literal: Cherishing the aim to aid the age, hoping for a lord with dragon countenance, he folded wings awaiting the season, watching for wind and clouds before moving.
translations.idiomatic: biding his time for a dragon-faced ruler worthy of his talent.

sentences.zh: 桓溫入關，猛被褐而詣之，一面談當世之事，捫虱而言，旁若無人。

translations.literal: When Huan Wen entered the pass, Meng in coarse clothes went to him; in one meeting they discussed the age's affairs; he picked lice while speaking, as if no one else were there.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen marched into Guanzhong, Wang Meng met him in homespun, spoke of statecraft while picking lice as coolly as if alone,

sentences.zh: 溫察而異之，問曰：「吾奉天子之命，率銳師十萬，杖義討逆，為百姓除殘賊，而三秦豪傑未有至者何也？

translations.literal: Wen observed him and thought him strange, asking, "We have received the Son of Heaven's command, leading a hundred thousand crack troops, relying on righteousness to punish rebels, removing cruel bandits for the black-haired people—yet the heroes of the three Qin have not come—why is that?"
translations.idiomatic: and Huan Wen asked why no Qin notables had rallied to his hundred-thousand-man crusade,

sentences.zh: 」猛曰：「公不遠數千里，深入寇境，長安咫尺而不渡灞水，百姓未見公心故也，所以不至。

translations.literal: Meng said, "You, sir, did not shrink from several thousand li, deeply entered bandit territory, yet Chang'an is within a foot and you do not cross the Ba waters—the common people have not seen your heart; that is why they do not come."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng answered that Huan Wen's refusal to ford the Ba and strike Chang'an showed the people he lacked true resolve,

sentences.zh: 」溫默然無以酬之。

translations.literal: Wen was silent and had nothing to answer.
translations.idiomatic: leaving Huan Wen speechless,

sentences.zh: 溫之將還，賜猛車馬，拜高官督護，請與俱南。

translations.literal: When Wen was about to return, he bestowed on Meng chariot and horses, appointed him senior chief protector, and asked him to go south together.
translations.idiomatic: who then offered Wang Meng rich gifts and a staff post to lure him south,

sentences.zh: 猛還山咨師，師曰：「卿與桓溫豈並世哉！

translations.literal: Meng returned to the mountain and consulted his teacher; the teacher said, "Can you and Huan Wen share one age!
translations.idiomatic: but Wang Meng's teacher asked whether he could ever share an era with Huan Wen,

sentences.zh: 在此自可富貴，何為遠乎！

translations.literal: Here you can naturally be rich and noble—why go far!"
translations.idiomatic: and said wealth and honor were already at hand in the north,

sentences.zh: 」猛乃止。

translations.literal: " Meng thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: so Wang Meng stayed,

sentences.zh: 苻堅將有大志，聞猛名，遣呂婆樓招之，一見便若平生。

translations.literal: Fu Jian was about to harbor a great aim; hearing Meng's name, he sent Lü Polou to summon him; at one meeting it was as if they had been friends all their lives.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian sought greatness, he sent Lü Polou to fetch Wang Meng; their first meeting felt like old friendship,

sentences.zh: 語及廢興大事，異符同契，若玄德之遇孔明也。

translations.literal: When speech reached the great matters of decline and rise, their tally matched though the tokens differed—like Xuande meeting Kongming.
translations.idiomatic: and their talk of rise and fall matched like Liu Bei meeting Zhuge Liang,

sentences.zh: 及堅僭位，以猛為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When Jian usurped the throne, he made Meng gentleman of the palace secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian appointed him palace secretariat gentleman on taking the throne,

sentences.zh: 時始平多枋頭西歸之人，豪右縱橫，劫盜充斥，乃轉猛為始平令。

translations.literal: At that time Pingyuan had many people returned west from Fangtou; powerful families ran rampant; robbery and banditry filled the place; therefore he transferred Meng to be magistrate of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: then sent him to magistrate Pingyuan, a county swarming with Fangtou veterans and bandit magnates,

sentences.zh: 猛下車，明法峻刑，澄察善惡，禁勒強豪。

translations.literal: Meng alighted from the carriage, clarified the laws and made punishments stern, clarified and examined good and evil, forbade and restrained the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: where he enforced harsh justice, sorted good from evil, and crushed local bullies,
