sentences.zh: 鞭殺一吏，百姓上書訟之，有司劾奏，檻車征下廷尉詔獄。

translations.literal: He flogged a clerk to death; the common people submitted memorials suing him; the responsible offices impeached him in memorial and summoned him in a cage cart down to the minister of justice's imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: until a flogged-to-death clerk triggered a lawsuit and his impeachment to imperial prison,

sentences.zh: 堅親問之，曰：「為政之體，德化為先，蒞任未幾而殺戮無數，何其酷也！

translations.literal: Jian personally questioned him, saying, "The body of government takes moral transformation as first; you have not been long in office yet killings are numberless—how is it so cruel!"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian personally challenged him for slaughtering so many so soon,

sentences.zh: 」猛曰：「臣聞宰甯國以禮，治亂邦以法。

translations.literal: Meng said, "Your subject has heard that one governs a tranquil state with ritual and a chaotic state with law.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng replied that orderly states need rites while ruined regions need law,

sentences.zh: 陛下不以臣不才，任臣以劇邑，謹為明君翦除凶猾。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, not deeming your subject untalented, assigned your subject to a harsh county; your subject carefully for a bright lord cuts away the fierce and slippery.
translations.idiomatic: and that Fu Jian had posted him to a violent border to cull predators for a wise sovereign,

sentences.zh: 始殺一奸，余尚萬數，若以臣不能窮殘盡暴，肅清軌法者，敢不甘心鼎鑊，以謝孤負。

translations.literal: I have killed one villain; those remaining still count in the myriads—if you hold that your subject cannot exhaust cruelty and violence and clear the tracks of the law, I dare not shrink from the cauldron and chopping block to answer for lone failure.
translations.idiomatic: adding that one execution left myriad villains and offering his own life if he failed to pacify the district,

sentences.zh: 酷政之刑，臣實未敢受之。

translations.literal: As for punishment for cruel government, your subject truly dares not accept it."
translations.idiomatic: but refusing the charge of cruel governance itself,

sentences.zh: 」堅謂群臣曰：「王景略固是夷吾、子產之儔也。

translations.literal: " Jian said to the host of ministers, "Wang Jinglue truly is of the same class as Yiwu and Zichan."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian then told the court Wang Meng rivaled Guan Zhong and Zichan,

sentences.zh: 」於是赦之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: and pardoned him,

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左丞、咸陽內史、京兆尹。

translations.literal: He was promoted left assistant of the secretariat, inner prefect of Xianyang, and metropolitan governor of the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: promoting him through capital posts,

sentences.zh: 未幾，除吏部尚書、太子詹事，又遷尚書左僕射、輔國將軍、司隸校尉，加騎都尉，居中宿衛。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed director of personnel and household supervisor to the heir apparent, again promoted left vice-director of the secretariat, general who aids the state, colonel director of retainer, added cavalry commandant, dwelling in the palace on night duty.
translations.idiomatic: then within a year to director of personnel, tutor to the crown prince, left vice-director, colonel of retainer, and imperial guard,

sentences.zh: 時猛年三十六，歲中五遷，權傾內外，宗戚舊臣皆害其寵。

translations.literal: At that time Meng was thirty-six; within the year he rose five posts; power tilted inside and outside; imperial kin and old ministers all envied his favor.
translations.idiomatic: five promotions in one year at age thirty-six made him the most powerful man at court and the target of envy,

sentences.zh: 尚書仇騰、丞相長史席寶數譖毀之，堅大怒，黜騰為甘松護軍，寶白衣領長史。

translations.literal: Director Qiu Teng and chief clerk of the chancellor Xi Bao several times slandered him; Jian was greatly angry, demoted Teng to Gansong guard general and made Bao commoner status acting chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: until Fu Jian banished Qiu Teng and humiliated Xi Bao for slandering him,

sentences.zh: 爾後上下咸服，莫有敢言。

translations.literal: After that above and below all submitted; none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: after which no one dared criticize Wang Meng,

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷尚書令、太子太傅，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Shortly he was promoted director of the secretariat, grand tutor to the heir apparent, added sanqi permanent attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he added director of the secretariat and grand tutor,

sentences.zh: 猛頻表累讓，堅竟不許。

translations.literal: Meng repeatedly memorialized declining, but Jian in the end did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: though Wang Meng repeatedly begged off,

sentences.zh: 又轉司徒、錄尚書事，余如故。

translations.literal: He was again transferred minister of education and recorder of affairs with the secretariat, the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian piled on minister of education and recorder of affairs,

sentences.zh: 猛辭以無功，不拜。

translations.literal: Meng declined on the ground of lacking merit and did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: which Wang Meng refused for want of merit,

sentences.zh: 後率諸軍討慕容暐，軍禁嚴明，師無私犯。

translations.literal: Later he led the various hosts to campaign against Murong Wei; army prohibitions were strict and clear; the army had no private violations.
translations.idiomatic: then led the conquest of Former Yan under iron discipline,

sentences.zh: 猛之未至鄴也，劫盜公行，及猛之至，遠近帖然，燕人安之。

translations.literal: Before Meng reached Ye, robbery went openly; when Meng arrived, far and near were quiet; Yan people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: so that banditry vanished the moment his army entered Ye,

sentences.zh: 軍還，以功進封清河郡侯，賜以美妾五人，上女妓十二人，中妓三十八人，馬百匹，車十乘。

translations.literal: When the army returned, by merit he was advanced enfeoffment to marquis of Qinghe commandery, granted five lovely concubines, twelve upper female entertainers, thirty-eight middle entertainers, a hundred horses, and ten carriages.
translations.idiomatic: earning a marquisate, concubines, musicians, horses, and carriages,

sentences.zh: 猛上疏固辭不受。

translations.literal: Meng submitted a memorial firmly declining and not accepting.
translations.idiomatic: all of which he tried to return,

sentences.zh: 時既留鎮冀州，堅遣猛於六州之內聽以便宜從事，簡召英俊，以補關東守宰，授訖，言台除正。

translations.literal: At that time he had been left to garrison Jizhou; Jian sent Meng within the six provinces to listen to convenience in handling affairs, to select and summon heroes to fill the passes east's prefects and magistrates; when appointment was finished, report to the secretariat for formal removal.
translations.idiomatic: while garrisoning Ji he held discretionary personnel power over six provinces to staff the northeast,

sentences.zh: 居數月，上疏曰：「臣前所以朝聞夕拜，不顧艱虞者，正以方難未夷，軍機權速，庶竭命戎行，甘驅馳之役，敷宣皇威，展筋骨之效，故僶俛從事，叨據負乘，可謂恭命于濟時，俟太平於今日。

translations.literal: After several months he submitted a memorial saying, "Your subject earlier therefore heard court in the morning and was appointed by evening, not caring for hardship and peril, was only because the region's difficulty was not yet pacified and military affairs were urgent on authority, hoping to exhaust life in the army, willingly accept the service of driving and galloping, spread and display imperial awe, extend the effect of sinews and bones—therefore stooping to the task, wrongly occupying the place of the overloaded cart—one may call it reverently obeying the order in a time of rescue, awaiting great peace in this day.
translations.idiomatic: he then memorialized that he had accepted rapid promotions only for wartime urgency,

sentences.zh: 今聖德格於皇天，威靈被於八表，弘化已熙，六合清泰，竊敢披貢丹誠，請避賢路。

translations.literal: Now sagely virtue matches August Heaven; awesome spirit covers the eight outer regions; great transformation already shines; the six directions are clear and tranquil—I dare privately spread out cinnabar sincerity and beg to yield the road to worthies.
translations.idiomatic: but now that the realm was pacified he begged to step aside for worthier men,

sentences.zh: 設官分職，各有司存，豈應孤任愚臣，以速傾敗！

translations.literal: Setting offices and dividing duties—each has its charge—how should one alone burden a foolish subject, thereby hastening overturn and defeat!
translations.idiomatic: arguing that fixed offices should not be monopolized by one minister,

sentences.zh: 東夏之事，非臣區區所能康理，願徙授親賢，濟臣顛墜。

translations.literal: The affairs of the eastern Xia are not what your subject, in his petty sphere, can peacefully order—I wish to shift appointment to kin and worthies to save your subject from toppling.
translations.idiomatic: that eastern China needed princely governors, not himself,

sentences.zh: 若以臣有鷹犬微勤，未忍捐棄者，乞待罪一州，效盡力命。

translations.literal: If because your subject has slight merit like a hawk or hound you cannot yet bear to cast me away, I beg to await punishment in one commandery and exhaust strength and life.
translations.idiomatic: or at most let him serve as a humble prefect,

sentences.zh: 徐方始賓，淮、汝防重，六州處分，府選便宜，輒以悉停。

translations.literal: Xu region has just submitted; Huai and Ru defenses are heavy; the six provinces' dispositions and prefectural selections on convenience—I rashly request all be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: and asked to end his extraordinary six-province personnel powers,

sentences.zh: 督任弗可虛曠，深願時降神規。

translations.literal: Supervisory duty cannot be left empty; I deeply hope the times will send down divine planning."
translations.idiomatic: begging Fu Jian to replace him before disaster struck,

sentences.zh: 」堅不許，遣其侍中梁讜詣鄴喻旨，猛乃視事如前。

translations.literal: " Jian did not permit it, sent his palace attendant Liang Dan to Ye to proclaim the intent, and Meng thereupon administered affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian refused, sent Liang Dan to Ye with the emperor's word, and Wang Meng stayed in office,

sentences.zh: 俄入為丞相、中書監、尚書令、太子太傅、司隸校尉，持節、常侍、將軍、侯如故。

translations.literal: Shortly he entered as chancellor, overseer of the secretariat, director of the secretariat, grand tutor to the heir apparent, colonel director of retainer—holding staff, permanent attendant, general, and marquis as before.
translations.idiomatic: soon summoning him to court as chancellor, secretariat overseer, and colonel while keeping his old titles,

sentences.zh: 稍加都督中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: Slightly added area commander-in-chief of all military affairs within and without.
translations.idiomatic: and added grand military command over all armies,

sentences.zh: 猛表讓久之。

translations.literal: Meng memorialized yielding for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng long declined the added command,

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「卿昔螭蟠布衣，朕龍潛弱冠，屬世事紛紜，厲士之際，顛覆厥德。

translations.literal: Jian said, "You, sir, once coiled as a chilong in common cloth; We, dragon submerged, in the weak-crown years—just when the world's affairs were tangled and the age sharpened gentlemen, overturned that virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian reminisced how they had met as obscure youths in chaotic times,

sentences.zh: 朕奇卿於暫見，擬卿為臥龍，卿亦異朕於一言，回《考槃》之雅志，豈不精契神交，千載之會！

translations.literal: We marveled at you, sir, on brief sight, likened you to the Crouching Dragon; you, sir, also marveled at Us in one phrase, turning the lofty aim of 'Kao Pan'—is it not subtle tally and spiritual communion, a meeting of a thousand ages!
translations.idiomatic: calling their bond a once-a-millennium match like Liu Bei and Zhuge Liang,

sentences.zh: 雖傅岩入夢，薑公悟兆，今古一時，亦不殊也。

translations.literal: Though Fu Yue entered a dream and Duke Jiang understood the omen—ancient and modern one moment—they are not different.
translations.idiomatic: likening them to King Wu's dream of Fu Yue and Jiang Ziya's omen,

sentences.zh: 自卿輔政，幾將二紀，內厘百揆，外蕩群凶，天下向定，彝倫始敘。

translations.literal: Since you, sir, have assisted government, nearly two twelve-year cycles—within you have ordered the hundred handles, without you have swept away the mass of villains; all under Heaven tends to stability; constant norms begin to be ordered.
translations.idiomatic: praising two dozen years of order at home and victory abroad,

sentences.zh: 朕且欲從容於上，望卿勞心於下，弘濟之務，非卿而誰！

translations.literal: We for the moment wish to take ease above and look to you, sir, to labor in heart below—the task of great rescue is none other than you, sir!"
translations.idiomatic: and begging Wang Meng to keep bearing the load,

sentences.zh: 」遂不許。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian refused every demurral,

sentences.zh: 其後數年，復授司徒。

translations.literal: Several years later he again appointed minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: and later pressed the minister of education title again,

sentences.zh: 猛復上疏曰：「臣聞乾象盈虛，惟後則之；

translations.literal: Meng again submitted a memorial saying, "Your subject has heard that the Qian image waxes and wanes—only the later follow it;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng cited cosmic cycles and proper matching of talent to office,

sentences.zh: 位稱以才，官非則曠。

translations.literal: Positions are titled by talent; if office does not match, it is empty.
translations.idiomatic: warning that titles without talent hollowed the state,

sentences.zh: 鄭武翼周，仍世載詠；

translations.literal: Duke Wu of Zheng aided Zhou and for generations carried song;
translations.idiomatic: praising Duke Wu of Zheng,

sentences.zh: 王叔昧寵，政替身亡，斯則成敗之殷監，為臣之炯戒。

translations.literal: Prince Shu misliked favor and government failed and he perished—these are then the bright mirror of success and failure, the blazing warning for ministers.
translations.idiomatic: contrasting the Western Zhou prince who fell from favor,

sentences.zh: 竊惟鼎宰崇重，參路太階，宜妙盡時賢，對揚休命。

translations.literal: Your subject privately thinks the tripod minister is lofty and weighty, treads the Grand Stairway's middle track—wonderfully it should exhaust the age's worthies to answer the splendid mandate.
translations.idiomatic: arguing the minister of education required a worthier man,

sentences.zh: 魏祖以文和為公，貽笑孫後；

translations.literal: Wei Taizu made Wenhe duke and left laughter to later Suns;
translations.idiomatic: citing Cao Cao's controversial choice of Jia Xu,

sentences.zh: 千秋一言致相，匈奴吲之。

translations.literal: Qianqiu with one phrase became minister—the Xiongnu sneered at it.
translations.idiomatic: and Han's minister Zhang Qianqiu mocked by the steppe,

sentences.zh: 臣何庸狷，而應斯舉！

translations.literal: How is your subject mean and petty yet fit for this elevation!
translations.idiomatic: protesting his own mediocrity,

sentences.zh: 不但取嗤鄰遠，實令為虜輕秦。

translations.literal: Not only will it fetch ridicule from neighbors afar—it truly will make captives despise Qin.
translations.idiomatic: fearing Jin would mock Qin for over-promoting him,

sentences.zh: 昔東野窮馭，顏子知其將弊。

translations.literal: In the past Dongye exhausted the team—Yan Hui knew the carriage would break.
translations.idiomatic: citing Confucius's parable of an over-driven chariot,

sentences.zh: 陛下不復料度臣之才力，私懼敗亡是及。

translations.literal: Your Majesty no longer measures your subject's talents and strength; your subject privately fears defeat and destruction will reach him.
translations.idiomatic: and warning he would break like Dongye's horses,

sentences.zh: 且上虧憲典，臣何顏處之！

translations.literal: Moreover it would fault the statutes above—what face has your subject to dwell in it!
translations.idiomatic: that accepting would shame the law,

sentences.zh: 雖陛下私臣，其如天下何！

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty favors your subject in private, what of all under Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: and that private favor could not answer the realm,

sentences.zh: 願回日月之鑒，矜臣後悔，使上無過授之謗，臣蒙覆燾之恩。

translations.literal: We beg you turn the sun and moon's mirror, pity your subject's later regret, so that above there is no slander of mistaken appointment and your subject receives the favor of covering shade."
translations.idiomatic: asking Fu Jian to revoke the edict to protect both throne and minister,

sentences.zh: 」堅竟不從。

translations.literal: " Jian in the end did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian still refused,

sentences.zh: 猛乃受命。

translations.literal: Meng thereupon received the command.
translations.idiomatic: so Wang Meng accepted,

sentences.zh: 軍國內外萬機之務，事無巨細，莫不歸之。

translations.literal: Of the myriad tasks of army and state, inside and outside, matters great and small, none did not return to him.
translations.idiomatic: and every civil and military decision passed through his hands,

sentences.zh: 猛宰政公平，流放屍素，拔幽滯，顯賢才，外修兵革，內綜儒學，勸課農桑，教以廉恥，無罪而不刑，無才而不任，庶績咸熙，百揆時敘。

translations.literal: Meng presided over government fairly, drifted away the walking corpses, raised the hidden and stuck, displayed worthies, without repaired arms without and synthesized Confucian learning within, urged farming and silkworms, taught with integrity and shame; none without guilt went unpunished, none without talent went unappointed—thus all duties shone and the hundred handles were timely ordered.
translations.idiomatic: where he purged drones, promoted talent, balanced war and culture, enforced law and agriculture until the machinery of state ran clear,

sentences.zh: 於是兵強國富，垂及升平，猛之力也。

sentences.zh: 吾將任汝以天下之事，奈何事事折吾，沮壞大謀！

translations.literal: We are about to entrust you, sir, with all under Heaven's affairs—why do you bend Us on every matter, blocking and ruining the great plan!
translations.idiomatic: and accusing Fu Rong of sabotaging his world conquest,

sentences.zh: 汝尚如此，況於眾乎！

translations.literal: If you are still thus, how much more the multitude!"
translations.idiomatic: asking how worse the crowd must be,

sentences.zh: 」堅之將入寇也，融又切切諫曰：「陛下聽信鮮卑、羌虜諂諛之言，採納良家少年利口之說，臣恐非但無成，亦大事去矣。

translations.literal: " When Jian was about to invade south, Rong again urgently remonstrated, saying, "Your Majesty listens to the flattering words of Xianbei and Qiang captives and adopts the clever talk of good-family youths—your subject fears not only no success but that the great matter is already lost.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the southern invasion Fu Rong warned that Xianbei, Qiang, and brash youths would ruin the campaign,

sentences.zh: 垂、萇皆我之仇敵，思聞風塵之變，冀因之以逞其凶德。

translations.literal: Chui and Chang are both Our enemies; they long to hear the turmoil of wind and dust, hoping by it to give rein to their vicious virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui and Yao Chang, he said, prayed for Qin's collapse,

sentences.zh: 少年等皆富足子弟，希關軍旅，苟說佞諂之言，以會陛下之意，不足采也。

translations.literal: The youths are all sons of rich houses who covet joining the army; they only speak sycophantic words to meet Your Majesty's mind—not worth adopting."
translations.idiomatic: and the noble youths were useless flatterers,

sentences.zh: 」堅弗納。

translations.literal: " Jian did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian ignored him,

sentences.zh: 及淮南之敗，垂、萇之叛，堅悼恨彌深。

translations.literal: When the defeat south of the Huai came and Chui and Chang rebelled, Jian's grief and regret grew deeper.
translations.idiomatic: until Feishui and the Murong-Yao revolts deepened Fu Jian's regret,

sentences.zh: 苻朗

translations.literal: Fu Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lang.

sentences.zh: 苻朗，字元達，堅之從兄子也。

translations.literal: Fu Lang, style Yuanda, was Jian's cousin's son.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lang, courtesy Yuanda, was Fu Jian's nephew,

sentences.zh: 性宏達，神氣爽邁，幼懷遠操，不屑時榮。

translations.literal: By nature he was magnanimous and far-reaching, spirit and bearing bright and bold; in youth he cherished lofty conduct and disdained the age's glory.
translations.idiomatic: open-minded and aloof from vulgar ambition,

sentences.zh: 堅嘗目之曰：「吾家千里駒也。

translations.literal: Jian once looked on him and said, "He is Our family's thousand-li foal."
translations.idiomatic: so Fu Jian called him the family's thousand-li colt,

sentences.zh: 」徵拜鎮東將軍、青州刺史，封樂安男，不得已起而就官。

translations.literal: " He was summoned general who garrisons the east and inspector of Qing province, enfeoffed baron of Le'an; unwillingly he rose and took office.
translations.idiomatic: then summoned to Qingzhou despite his reluctance,

sentences.zh: 及為方伯，有若素士，耽玩經籍，手不釋卷，每談虛語玄，不覺日之將夕；

translations.literal: When he became a regional lord he was like a plain scholar—he delighted in classics, hand never releasing the scroll; whenever he discoursed on emptiness and spoke on mystery, he did not notice the day nearing evening;
translations.idiomatic: governing like a scholar, lost in books and abstruse talk until nightfall,

sentences.zh: 登涉山水，不知老之將至。

translations.literal: climbing hills and fording streams, he did not know old age would come.
translations.idiomatic: hiking mountains unaware of age,

sentences.zh: 在任甚有稱績。

translations.literal: In office he had very praised achievement.
translations.idiomatic: and earning praise in office,

sentences.zh: 後晉遣淮陰太守高素伐青州，朗遣使詣謝玄于彭城求降，玄表朗許之，詔加員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Later Jin sent Huaiyin prefect Gao Su to campaign against Qing province; Lang sent envoys to Xie Xuan at Pengcheng to request surrender; Xuan memorialized Lang and permitted it; an edict added supernumerary sanqi gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: surrendering Qing to Jin's Gao Su via Xie Xuan and receiving a Jin sinceure,

sentences.zh: 既至揚州，風流邁于一時，超然自得，志陵萬物，所與悟言，不過一二人而已。

translations.literal: When he reached Yangzhou his refinement surpassed the age—aloof and self-content, his aim overtopping the myriad things; those with whom he had awakened speech were no more than one or two.
translations.idiomatic: he cut a singular figure in Yangzhou, condescending to almost everyone,

sentences.zh: 驃騎長史王忱，江東之俊秀，聞而詣之，朗稱疾不見。

translations.literal: Chief clerk of the chariot-and-horse Wang Chen, the east's outstanding talent, heard and visited him; Lang claimed illness and did not see him.
translations.idiomatic: snubbing even the brilliant Wang Chen,

sentences.zh: 沙門釋法汰問朗曰：「見王吏部兄弟未？

translations.literal: The monk Shi Fatuo asked Lang, "Have you seen Wang the personnel director's brothers?"
translations.idiomatic: until monk Fatuo asked if he had met the Wang brothers,

sentences.zh: 」朗曰：「吏部為誰？

translations.literal: Lang said, "Who is the personnel director?
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lang replied, 'Which personnel director?',

sentences.zh: 非人面而狗心、狗面而人心兄弟者乎？

translations.literal: Are they not the brothers with human faces and dog hearts, and dog faces and human hearts?"
translations.idiomatic: calling them men with dogs' hearts and dogs with men's faces,

sentences.zh: 」王忱醜而才慧，國寶美貌而才劣于弟，故朗雲然。

translations.literal: Wang Chen was ugly but talented and clever; Wang Guobao was handsome but less talented than his younger brother—therefore Lang spoke thus.
translations.idiomatic: mocking ugly clever Wang Chen and handsome dull Wang Guobao,

sentences.zh: 汰悵然自失。

translations.literal: Fatuo was disappointed and lost.
translations.idiomatic: leaving Fatuo speechless,

sentences.zh: 其忤物侮人，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His offending things and insulting people were all of this class.
translations.idiomatic: such insults typified his arrogance,

sentences.zh: 謝安常設宴請之，朝士盈坐，並機褥壺席。

translations.literal: Xie An often set feasts inviting him; court gentlemen filled the seats, together with low tables, cushions, pots, and mats.
translations.idiomatic: when Xie An feasted him amid packed ministers and floor mats.

sentences.zh: 朗每事欲誇之，唾則令小兒跪而張口，既唾而含出，頃復如之，坐者為不及之遠也。

translations.literal: Lang in every matter wished to flaunt it; when he spat he ordered a child to kneel and open the mouth; after spitting he had them hold it out; shortly he did again—those seated felt they could not match how far he carried such things.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lang turned every habit into a spectacle: he made boys kneel with mouths open to receive his spit, then spit again, leaving guests unable to rival his outrageousness,

sentences.zh: 又善識味，咸酢及肉皆別所由。

translations.literal: He was also good at discerning flavors—salt, vinegar, and meats he could all distinguish as to origin.
translations.idiomatic: and claimed he could taste the provenance of salt, vinegar, and every cut of meat,

sentences.zh: 會稽王司馬道子為朗設盛饌，極江左精肴。

translations.literal: Prince of Kuaiji Sima Daozi set a lavish feast for Lang, exhausting the finest dishes south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: when Sima Daozi laid a banquet of Jiangzuo's finest,

sentences.zh: 食訖，問曰：「關中之食孰若此？

translations.literal: When eating finished, he asked, "How does food in Guanzhong compare to this?"
translations.idiomatic: he asked how Guanzhong cuisine compared,

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「皆好，惟鹽味小生耳。

translations.literal: He answered, "All are good; only the salt flavor is slightly 'raw.'"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lang allowed that everything was excellent but the salt tasted a shade under-cured,

sentences.zh: 」既問宰夫，皆如其言。

translations.literal: When they questioned the cooks, all was as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: and kitchen staff confirmed each detail,

sentences.zh: 或人殺雞以食之，既進，朗曰：「此雞棲恆半露。

translations.literal: Someone killed a chicken to serve him; when it came forward, Lang said, "This chicken's roost was always half exposed."
translations.idiomatic: tasting a chicken, he declared its coop had been half open to the weather,

sentences.zh: 」檢之，皆驗。

translations.literal: They checked it—all verified.
translations.idiomatic: and inspection proved him right,

sentences.zh: 又食鵝肉，知黑白之處。

translations.literal: Again he ate goose meat and knew the places of the white and black.
translations.idiomatic: with goose he could map every patch of dark and light meat,

sentences.zh: 人不信，記而試之，無豪厘之差。

translations.literal: People did not believe; they marked it and tested—there was not a hair's breadth of error.
translations.idiomatic: skeptics who marked cuts found him exact to a hair,

sentences.zh: 時人咸以為知味。

translations.literal: Men of the time all thought him one who knew flavor.
translations.idiomatic: so contemporaries hailed him as a connoisseur,

sentences.zh: 後數年，王國寶譖而殺之。

translations.literal: Several years later Wang Guobao slandered him and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: until Wang Guobao's slander brought his execution,

sentences.zh: 王忱將為荊州刺史，待殺朗而後發。

translations.literal: Wang Chen was about to become inspector of Jing province and waited to kill Lang before setting out.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen delayed his Jingzhou posting until Fu Lang was dead,

sentences.zh: 臨刑，志色自若，為詩曰：「四大起何因？

translations.literal: Facing execution, his intent and color were as if normal; he composed a poem, saying, "From what cause do the four greats arise?
translations.idiomatic: At the block he stayed composed, composing verse on Buddhist themes,

sentences.zh: 聚散無窮已。

translations.literal: Gathering and scattering have no end.
translations.idiomatic: on gathering and scattering without end,

sentences.zh: 既過一生中，又入一死理。

translations.literal: Having passed through one life, again entering one death's principle.
translations.idiomatic: on leaving one life for death's realm,

sentences.zh: 冥心乘和暢，未覺有終始。

translations.literal: Darkening the mind, riding harmony and ease, one does not feel there is beginning or end.
translations.idiomatic: on resting in equanimity beyond beginnings and ends,

sentences.zh: 如何箕山夫，奄焉處東市！

translations.literal: How is it that a husband of Mount Ji—suddenly ends at the eastern market!"
translations.idiomatic: lamenting that a recluse like Mount Ji's sage should die at the execution ground,

sentences.zh: 曠此百年期，遠同嵇叔子。

translations.literal: Leaving this hundred-year span, far matching Uncle Ji's son.
translations.idiomatic: likening his fate to Ji Shao's,

sentences.zh: 命也歸自天，委化任冥紀。

translations.literal: Fate returns to Heaven; entrust transformation to the dark reckoner."
translations.idiomatic: and resigning fate to Heaven's dark ledger,

sentences.zh: 」著《苻子》數十篇行於世，亦《老》《莊》之流也。

translations.literal: He wrote several tens of chapters of the Master Fu, current in the world—also of the class of the Laozi and Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: His collected essays, the Master Fu, circulated in the Zhuangzi tradition.
